messages.content: Please write a thank-you note, about 50 words, to my friend Ritu. She lent me her camera for my school project and it helped me a lot.

Dear Ritu,
Thank you so much for lending me your camera. The photos turned out beautifully, and my teacher loved the project. I took good care of it and have returned it with a full battery. You are a true friend. Let's go for ice cream soon, my treat!
Love,
Anil
I broke my brother's toy car by mistake. Write a short sorry note I can leave on his bed, about 45 words.

Dear Rohan,
I am really sorry that I broke your red toy car. I was playing with it and dropped it on the floor. I did not mean to hurt it. Please let me buy you a new one with my pocket money.
Your brother,
Kabir
Write a congratulations message, around 50 words, for my neighbour Mrs. Gomes, whose son won a gold medal in swimming.

Dear Mrs. Gomes,
Warm congratulations to you and your family! We heard that Joel won the gold medal in swimming. He worked so hard, and we saw him leave for practice every morning. You must be very proud. Please give him our best wishes.
Regards,
The Menon family
A classmate of mine, Tanvi, is at home with a bad cold. Write a get-well note from the whole class, about 50 words.

Dear Tanvi,
We miss you in class! The room is quieter without your jokes. Please rest well and do not worry about the lessons, because we will share our notes with you. Get well soon and come back with a big smile.
From all your friends in Class 7B
Write a short reminder message for my team about submitting the monthly report by Thursday evening. Around 40 words.

Hello team,
This is a friendly reminder to send in your monthly reports by Thursday evening. Please check your numbers once before you submit. If you need any help, message me today so we can fix it together.
Thanks,
Divya
Write an invitation, about 60 words, for my daughter Ishita's 7th birthday party. It is on Sunday at 4 pm at Green Park Club, and the theme is jungle animals.

You are invited!
Ishita is turning seven, and we are having a jungle party. Come dressed as your favourite animal, and get ready for games, a treasure hunt and cake.
Date: Sunday
Time: 4 pm
Place: Green Park Club
Please let us know if you can join us. We can't wait to see you!
Warm regards,
Sunita and Prakash
Write an invitation for parents to our school's science fair, about 55 words. It is on Friday, 10 am, in the main hall.

Dear Parents,
Our students request the pleasure of your company at the Annual Science Fair. Children from Classes 5 to 8 will show their working models and experiments. Your visit will encourage them greatly.
Date: Friday
Time: 10 am
Venue: Main Hall
Tea will be served after the exhibition.
Yours sincerely,
Mrs. D'Souza, Science Coordinator
Write a casual invite, asking friends to come over for a board game night at my place on Saturday evening. About 50 words.

Hey everyone,
It's board game night at my place this Saturday, from 6 pm onwards. I have Ludo, Carrom and a very old Monopoly set. Bring your own snacks and your competitive spirit! Tea and cold drinks are on me. Please tell me by Friday if you're coming.
See you soon,
Neha
Our family is hosting a small Navratri garba evening. Write an invitation to the neighbours, about 50 words.

Dear Neighbours,
We are hosting a small garba evening for Navratri this Saturday at 7 pm in our building courtyard. Please come with your family and join us in the dance. Dandiya sticks will be provided, and there will be sweets for everyone. We would love to celebrate with you.
Warm wishes,
The Patel family
I'm captain of our colony cricket team. Write a message inviting new players to trial matches this Sunday, around 50 words.

Hello cricket lovers!
Our colony team is looking for new players. Trial matches will be held this Sunday at 7 am on the ground behind the temple. Boys and girls of all ages are welcome, whether you bat, bowl or just love the game. Bring your own water bottle.
Captain Vikram
Please write a polite request to my school principal asking for permission to use the library after school hours to prepare for exams. Around 60 words. I'm Meena of Class 10.

Respected Sir,
I am Meena of Class 10. Our board exams are close, and I find it hard to study at home because of noise. I request you to kindly allow me and a few classmates to use the school library for one hour after classes. We will keep the place clean and quiet.
Thank you,
Meena, Class 10
Write a polite complaint to our building's watchman about people parking in front of my gate. Around 55 words, no anger.

Dear Bhaiya,
I hope you are well. For the last few days, some cars have been parked in front of my gate, and I cannot take my scooter out. Could you please ask visitors to use the parking area instead? I understand it is a busy time for you. Thank you for your help.
Regards,
Mr. Kulkarni, Flat 12
A tailor stitched my daughter's school uniform too short and has not fixed it. Write a firm but polite complaint message, about 65 words.

Dear Sir,
I collected my daughter's school uniform from your shop last Monday, and the skirt is much shorter than the size we gave. I showed it to you the next day, and you promised to alter it within two days. It has been a week now. Please fix it by Saturday, as school reopens on Monday. Thank you.
Mrs. Fernandes
Draft a mail to my teacher, Mr. Iyer, saying I could not submit my history project on time because I was unwell, and asking for two more days. Around 75 words. I'm Zoya from Class 9.

Subject: Request for extension on history project

Dear Mr. Iyer,
I am Zoya from Class 9. I could not submit my history project yesterday because I was not well and stayed at home for two days. The project is almost ready, and I only need to finish the last chapter. May I please have two more days to submit it? I am sorry for the trouble.
Thank you for understanding.
Yours sincerely,
Zoya
I need to ask my manager, Ms. Rao, for a day off next Friday for my cousin's wedding. Write the email, about 85 words. I'm Imran, and my current work will be finished by Thursday.

Subject: Leave request for Friday

Dear Ms. Rao,
I hope you are doing well. I would like to request a day of leave next Friday, as I must attend my cousin's wedding. I will complete my current tasks by Thursday and send you the final files before I leave. I have also spoken to Sana, who can handle any urgent queries during my absence. Kindly confirm if this works for you.
Thank you,
Imran
Please email my neighbour Mr. Desai about the noise from his terrace parties late at night. Polite, about 75 words. I'm Kavya from the flat below.

Subject: A small request about evening noise

Dear Mr. Desai,
I am Kavya from the flat below yours. We enjoy hearing the cheer on your terrace, but the music has continued past midnight on weekends, and my father cannot sleep well. Could you please lower the volume after ten at night? I would be very grateful. Thank you for being such a kind neighbour.
Best wishes,
Kavya
Draft a notice for the school notice board about a change in the bus timing next week. Buses leave 30 minutes earlier on Monday and Tuesday. About 55 words.

NOTICE
Change in Bus Timing

All students who use the school bus are informed that the buses will leave thirty minutes earlier than usual on Monday and Tuesday next week. Please reach your bus stop on time. Parents are requested to make a note of this. Normal timings will resume from Wednesday.

By order,
Transport Office
Write a notice for our apartment lift, around 65 words, saying that it will be under repair on Wednesday from 10 am to 1 pm.

NOTICE TO ALL RESIDENTS

The lift will be closed for repair on Wednesday from 10 am to 1 pm. During this time, please use the stairs. Elderly residents and families with small children who need help may call the security desk, and someone will assist them. We are sorry for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.

Secretary, Sunrise Apartments
Write a notice inviting local residents to a tree-planting morning in our park on Sunday, 7 am. About 70 words.

TREE-PLANTING MORNING

Join us this Sunday at 7 am in Rose Garden Park, as we plant thirty saplings together. Neem, jamun and gulmohar are waiting for new homes. Bring a hat, a water bottle and your family. Spades and saplings will be provided. Children are especially welcome. Let us make our neighbourhood greener, one tree at a time.

Garden Welfare Group
Describe a tea stall by the roadside on a rainy evening in about 80 words.

The tea stall sits under a faded blue tarpaulin by the road. Rain drums on the sheet as customers crowd close, holding their bags over their heads. The owner pours milky tea from a dented kettle into small glasses. Steam rises and smells of ginger and cardamom. A stove glows orange, and plates of hot pakoras are passed around. Nobody is in a hurry now. Outside, the street shines wet and grey, but here, it is warm.
Describe the sound of a thunderstorm arriving over a village, around 70 words.

First, the wind rises and shakes the leaves. Dogs bark, and mothers call the children inside. Then a low rumble rolls across the fields, like a giant moving furniture in the sky. The thunder grows louder until the windows rattle. A flash of light lights up the lane, and big drops begin to fall on the tin roofs. Soon the whole village is filled with the loud, happy sound of rain.
Describe a Christmas midnight mass in a small church in Goa. About 90 words, please.

The little church stands white and shining under the stars. Inside, hundreds of candles glow, and the air smells of wax and fresh flowers. Families sit close together in their best clothes, the children yawning but excited. The choir begins to sing, and the old carols fill the hall softly. A small crib stands near the altar with a tiny baby in the straw. When the bells ring at midnight, everyone smiles and hugs. Outside, the village lights twinkle, and the night feels peaceful.
Write about 80 words describing a vegetable market early in the morning.

Before sunrise, the vegetable market is already awake. Carts roll in loaded with fresh spinach, bright tomatoes and long green beans. Sellers arrange their heaps carefully and sprinkle water to keep everything fresh. Voices call out prices, and scales clink. Buyers walk slowly, pinching tomatoes and smelling coriander. A porter hurries by with a basket on his head. The ground is wet and muddy, and the whole place smells of earth and green leaves.
Write a description of a very hot afternoon in a small town in exactly five sentences.

The sun hangs high and bright over the small town, and the tar on the road shines like a black mirror. Shops pull down their shutters, and even the stray dogs lie still in the shade. A lonely ice-cream cart rings its bell and is soon surrounded by sweating schoolchildren. Ceiling fans turn slowly in the houses, giving little relief. By evening, a gentle breeze comes, and the whole town sighs in thanks.
Diary entry wanted: about 90 words, from a boy who got selected for the school football team today.

Tuesday, 14 March

Dear Diary,
I can hardly write because my hands are still shaking! The coach read out the team list after practice, and my name was there. I am in the school football team! I ran all the way home and told Ma, who hugged me and made halwa. Dad said he will come to my first match. I must practise my passing every day now. Tonight, I will sleep with my football next to my bed.
A girl lost her pet rabbit today. Write her diary entry, about 80 words.

Dear Diary,
Today was a sad day. When I woke up, Snowy did not come running to the door of his cage. Mummy sat with me and said he had grown old and had gone to sleep forever. I cried for a long time. Then we buried him under the guava tree, and I put a small flower on top. I will always remember how he nibbled my fingers. Goodnight, Snowy.
Can you write about 90 words in diary form for someone on the first night of a long train journey across India.

Dear Diary,
I am writing this on the upper berth, with the train rocking me gently. Outside, small stations flash by with yellow lights and sleepy tea-sellers. An aunty below me shared her thepla, and we talked for an hour. The little boy opposite taught me a card game. I never thought a train could feel so friendly. The wheels make a steady song, and my eyes are getting heavy. Tomorrow, we will wake up in a new state.
I'd like a diary entry, about 100 words, by a young woman after her first day as a teacher in a village school.

Dear Diary,
Today I stood in front of my first class. Thirty small faces looked at me, and my heart was beating so loudly. I forgot half of what I had planned, so I simply asked each child her name and her favourite food. We laughed a lot. A girl named Basanti gave me a wildflower and said, "Teacher, you smell like the market." I did not know whether to laugh or cry. I am tired, but I feel happy. I think I will love this place.
Write a tiny story for children, about 100 words, about a little cloud who is afraid to rain.

Once there was a little cloud called Pippa who was afraid to rain. "If I rain, I will disappear," she said. The other clouds floated away, and Pippa stayed alone above a dry brown field. Below, a farmer looked up and sighed, and the flowers hung their heads. Pippa felt sorry for them. She took a deep breath and let one small drop fall. Then another. Soon the field was green and the flowers danced. Pippa was still there, and she was fluffier and happier than ever.
Tell me a short story for young kids, about 100 words, about a squirrel who forgets where he hid his nuts.

Sonu the squirrel hid his nuts all over the park before winter. But when the cold days came, he could not remember where he had put them. He looked under the bench and behind the swing, and found nothing. His tummy rumbled. Then his friend Mina the sparrow said, "Look at the big banyan tree." Sonu dug at its roots and found a pile of nuts! There, a new little tree was also growing from one he had forgotten. Sonu smiled. "I planted a tree by mistake," he said happily.
I need a story for my class's reading hour, about 100 words, about a girl who is scared of speaking on stage but finally does it.

Anaya loved reading poems aloud at home, but on stage her voice always disappeared. When her teacher chose her for the annual day speech, her hands turned cold. At night she practised in front of her teddy bear. On the big day, she looked at the crowd and her mind went blank. Then she saw her little brother in the front row, waving at her. She smiled and began. Her voice shook at first, then grew strong. When she finished, everyone clapped loudly. Anaya had done it.
Write a short paragraph of about 80 words on why drinking water from a clean bottle is better than buying many plastic ones.

A reusable bottle is a small choice that makes a big difference. Plastic bottles are used once and then thrown away, and they often end up in drains and rivers. A steel or glass bottle can be filled again and again for years. It saves money, too, because you do not have to keep buying water. Just wash it every day and carry it with you. It is an easy way to keep our streets and our planet cleaner.
Write a paragraph for my class essay on 'Why Grandparents Are Special', about 80 words.

Grandparents are special because they have time for us. They tell stories of old days, teach us songs, and share recipes that have been in the family for years. When we are scolded, they quietly take our side. They remind us where we come from and how to be kind. A hug from a grandparent feels warm and safe. I am lucky to have mine, and I try to visit them as often as I can.
Write a short paragraph, around 70 words, on why playing outdoors is good for children.

Playing outdoors is good for children in many ways. They run, jump and climb, and that makes their bodies strong. They learn to share and to take turns when they play team games. Fresh air and sunshine make them feel cheerful. They also meet friends and discover how fun life is without a screen. After a long afternoon outside, children are tired, hungry and happy, and they sleep well at night.
Write a short rhyme for kids, four lines, about a rainy day.

Pitter-patter, drip and drop,
Rain is falling, will not stop.
Splash, splash, in my boots I go,
Puddles jumping, to and fro!
Write a simple poem, 4 lines, about a sleepy cat in the sun.

The cat lies down in a golden beam,
And blinks her eyes as if in a dream.
She stretches long and gives a yawn,
Then purrs herself to sleep till dawn.
Could you write a short poem for my mother for her birthday? Simple words, about 50 words.

Dear Amma, you wake before the sun,
You smile until the day is done.
You cook with love, you hold my hand,
You always seem to understand.
Today is yours, so rest and cheer,
You are the best, my mother dear.
Happy birthday! May every year
Bring joy and laughter, always near.
Make a funny rhyme for children, six lines, about a boy who loves mangoes.

Manu loved mangoes, big and sweet,
He ate them standing on his feet.
He ate them morning, noon and night,
His face was yellow, what a sight!
His mother laughed, "Dear Manu, stop!"
Then he ate one more and went plop!
Write a short note of encouragement, about 50 words, for my friend who failed her driving test the first time.

Dear Pooja,
Please do not feel bad about the test. Many people need a second try, and each try teaches us something. You are a careful driver, and I am sure you will pass next time. Let's celebrate with samosas when you do!
Your friend,
Leela
Say thank you to my manager, Mr. Khan, for supporting me during a hard month. About 50 words.

Dear Mr. Khan,
I want to thank you for your support this month. When the workload was heavy, you listened and helped me plan my time. I truly appreciate your patience and kindness. It made a hard month much easier, and I learnt a great deal from you.
With gratitude,
Sheetal
Write a thank-you note, about 45 words, to a neighbour who brought us soup when my mother was unwell. Don't mention any medical details.

Dear Mrs. Bhatt,
Thank you so much for the soup you sent us yesterday. It was warm and tasty, and we all enjoyed it. Your kindness meant a lot to us during a busy week. We are lucky to have such a caring neighbour.
Warm regards,
Sameer and family
Write a postcard message from Darjeeling to my grandmother, about 55 words.

Dear Ajji,
Greetings from Darjeeling! The hills are green and misty, and the tea gardens look like soft carpets. This morning we rode the toy train, and I waved at everyone. I ate hot momos and bought you a small woollen cap. I miss you and will tell you more stories when I come home.
Love,
Pranav
Write a polite message to my friend asking him to return the cricket bat I lent him last month. About 50 words.

Hi Arjun,
I hope you are well. I wanted to ask about my cricket bat, which I lent you last month. Our school match is on Saturday, and I would like to practise with it before that. Could you please bring it to school tomorrow? Thanks a lot!
Ravi
Email my class teacher, Mrs. Thomas, and ask her which chapters will be in the maths test on Monday. I'm Aarav from Class 6. About 60 words.

Subject: Question about Monday's maths test

Dear Mrs. Thomas,
I am Aarav from Class 6. I could not note down the chapters for Monday's maths test because I was late leaving class. Could you please tell me which chapters will be included? I want to prepare well. Thank you for your time.
Yours sincerely,
Aarav
Write a 60-word paragraph on why it is nice to help in the kitchen on a Sunday.

Helping in the kitchen on a Sunday is a joy. Sundays are slow, so the whole family has time to cook together. You can wash the vegetables, stir the dal, or roll out the dough. You learn useful skills and get to taste everything first. Best of all, you spend time with your family, and the food somehow tastes better when you have made it yourself.
Describe fireworks on Diwali night in about 70 words, for little children.

When it gets dark on Diwali, the sky becomes a big painting. Whoosh! A rocket goes up and bursts into red stars. Boom! Then come green and golden flowers that fall slowly. The little sparklers fizz in our hands and make tiny circles of light. Every house has rows of tiny lamps. Everyone shouts, "Wow!" We clap our hands and hold our ears. Diwali is a night of light and joy.
Write a message to my roommates reminding them that the gas cylinder needs to be booked this weekend. About 50 words.

Hi all,
A quick reminder that our gas cylinder is almost empty. Could one of us please book a new one this weekend? I booked the last one, so it would be great if someone else could do it this time. Please reply here once it is done. Thanks, everyone!
Shruti
We ordered a family dinner from a local restaurant and the rice was cold and one dish was missing. Write a polite complaint, about 60 words, to the manager.

Dear Manager,
We ordered a family dinner from your restaurant yesterday evening. When it arrived, the rice was cold, and the paneer dish we asked for was missing. We have enjoyed your food before, so we were surprised. Could you please look into this and let us know how it can be put right? Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Mohan Reddy
Please write a story for young children, about 100 words, about a firefly who is afraid of the dark.

Chintu the firefly lived in a big mango tree. All his friends glowed bright at night, but Chintu was afraid of the dark and hid in a leaf. "I can't go out," he said. One night, a baby bird fell from its nest and cried in the black garden. Nobody could see it. Chintu shook with fear, but he flew down and began to glow. His little light showed the way to the nest. The mother bird hugged him. From then on, Chintu was never afraid of the dark again.
Write a short notice, about 45 words, saying the school library will be closed on the day of the Holi holiday and will reopen the next day.

NOTICE

The school library will remain closed on the day of the Holi holiday. It will reopen the next day at the usual time. Students who have books due on the closed day may return them after the holiday without any fine. Happy Holi to all!

Librarian
Thank my friend Maya's parents for having me stay over at their house during the holidays. Around 50 words, from me, Tara.

Dear Uncle and Aunty,
Thank you for letting me stay at your home last week. The food was delicious, and I loved the evening walks and the card games. You made me feel like part of the family. Please tell Maya I will miss her. I hope I can return the kindness soon.
With love,
Tara
I spilled juice on my friend Harsh's library book. Help me write a short apology message, around 45 words.

Hi Harsh,
I am really sorry about your library book. I spilled juice on it while reading in the canteen, and a few pages are stained. I will talk to the librarian and pay for any damage. I feel terrible about it. Please forgive me.
Yours,
Dev
My cousin Neelam just had a baby girl. Please write a joyful message of congratulations, about 50 words.

Dear Neelam,
Congratulations on your beautiful baby girl! We are so happy for you and your husband. May she bring you lots of laughter and sweet, sleepy cuddles. We cannot wait to meet her and hold her tiny hands. Please send us photos soon.
All our love,
Aunt Rekha and Uncle Sanjay
Write a get-well message, around 45 words, for my grandfather, who is resting at home after a knee operation. Keep it cheerful and don't give any medical advice.

Dear Dada,
We are thinking of you every day and sending you lots of love. The house feels quiet without your stories and your loud laugh. Rest well, and we will bring your favourite jalebis on Sunday. Come back to your old self soon!
Your grandchildren
Write a reminder note for my son to carry his umbrella and lunch box to school tomorrow. Short, about 35 words, and friendly.

Good morning, Aman!
Please remember your umbrella today, because the sky looks cloudy. Your lunch box is on the table, and I have packed your favourite parathas. Have a lovely day at school!
Love,
Mummy
Write a congratulation message, about 50 words, to my colleague Farah on getting her first job promotion.

Dear Farah,
Congratulations on your promotion! You have earned it with your hard work and your kind nature. All of us have seen how carefully you handle every task, and how you always help new people. We are very proud of you. Let's have a small treat together this week to celebrate.
Warm wishes,
Gaurav
Write a thank-you note from the whole class to our teacher Mr. Das after a wonderful school trip to the museum. About 55 words.

Dear Mr. Das,
Thank you for taking us to the museum yesterday. We loved the old coins and the giant dinosaur skeleton. You answered all our questions patiently, even the silly ones. We learnt so much more than we do in class. It was the best trip of the year. Please take us again soon!
Your students,
Class 6C
My cricket ball broke my neighbour Mr. Pillai's flower pot. Write a sorry note, about 50 words, that I can leave at his door.

Dear Mr. Pillai,
I am very sorry that my cricket ball broke your flower pot yesterday. We should not have played so near your house. I have bought a new pot and planted a fresh flower in it. I will be more careful from now on. Please forgive me.
Sincerely,
Karthik, Flat 4
Write a note to remind my sister to return the library books on Friday. About 50 words, and make it a bit funny.

Dear Sis,
Alert! Alert! Your library books are begging to go home on Friday. They are tired of living under your bed. If you forget, you may have to pay a fine, and I will never let you forget it. Please save them, and your pocket money!
Your loving brother
Please write a note, about 45 words, thanking my aunt for the lovely sweater she knitted for me.

Dear Masi,
Thank you for the beautiful blue sweater. It fits perfectly, and it is so soft and warm. I wore it to school today, and all my friends admired it. I know you put hours of love into it. I will treasure it always.
Love,
Pia
Write an invitation to our housewarming puja, about 55 words. We are the Joshi family, moving into a new flat on Saturday at 10 am.

Dear Friends and Family,
We have moved into our new home, and we would be delighted to have you share this joy. We are holding a small housewarming puja on Saturday at 10 am. Lunch will follow. Your blessings and presence will make the day special. Please come and bring your smiles.
With warm regards,
The Joshi family, Flat 305, Lotus Heights
Invite everyone to a farewell lunch, about 65 words, for our colleague Mr. Nair, who retires on Friday. Lunch is in the office canteen at 1 pm.

Dear Colleagues,
After thirty happy years with us, Mr. Nair retires this Friday. Please join us in the canteen at 1 pm for a farewell lunch in his honour. Come and share your favourite memories of him. A small gift is being collected, and anyone who wishes may give a small amount to Priya at the front desk.
Warm regards,
The Staff Club
Draft an invitation, about 60 words, to an old-students reunion at our school next month. Date: second Saturday. Time: 4 pm. Tea and snacks.

Dear Friends,
Remember the long corridors, the bell, and the stolen mangoes from the school tree? We are bringing everyone back together for an Old Students' Reunion on the second Saturday of next month at 4 pm. Come and meet your classmates and teachers, and relive the best days of your life. Tea and snacks will be served.
See you there!
Alumni Committee
Write a short message inviting my friends to fly kites with me on the terrace on Makar Sankranti morning. About 50 words.

Hello friends,
Come and fly kites with me on our terrace this Makar Sankranti morning! We will start at eight with tea and tilgul laddoos. I have bought lots of colourful kites and strong thread. It will be a fun day full of sunshine and cheering. Please be there on time!
Anita
Help me invite our neighbours to a Lohri bonfire in the society garden on Thursday at 7 pm. Around 55 words, with a warm tone.

Dear Neighbours,
Join us for a Lohri bonfire in the society garden this Thursday at 7 pm. Let us gather around the fire, sing folk songs and share peanuts, popcorn and gajak. Children can bring their own small blankets. We hope the warmth of the fire and of friendship will brighten the cold evening. Everyone is welcome!
The Garden Committee
Write a polite complaint to a bus company because my long-distance bus came three hours late and no one told us anything. Around 60 words. I'm Naveen Gupta.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I travelled on your night bus to Jaipur last Friday. It arrived three hours late, and we received no information at the stop. Many passengers, including elderly people, were left waiting in the cold. I request you to look into the reasons and to inform passengers in future. Thank you for your attention.
Yours faithfully,
Naveen Gupta
Write a letter to my landlord asking him to repair the leaking tap in our kitchen. Polite, about 55 words. I'm Rohini, tenant of Flat 2B.

Dear Sir,
I hope you are well. The kitchen tap in Flat 2B has been leaking for a week, and water is wasted all day. Could you please send a plumber at your earliest convenience? I am at home in the evenings and can let the person in. Thank you very much for your help.
Regards,
Rohini
I ordered a glass vase and it came broken in the parcel. Write a polite complaint to the courier company, about 60 words, asking for a solution.

Dear Customer Care,
I received a parcel from your company yesterday, and the glass vase inside was broken. The box itself was torn at one corner. I have taken photos of it and kept the packing. I request you to investigate the matter and tell me how I can get a replacement or a refund. Thank you for your help.
Sincerely,
Lalitha Rao
Write a request to my class teacher asking if I can change my seat because I cannot see the board well from the back. Around 50 words. I'm Yash.

Dear Ma'am,
I am Yash of Class 8. I am sitting in the last row, and I cannot see the board clearly. Could you please let me move to a seat nearer the front? I promise to sit quietly and listen carefully. Thank you very much for your kindness.
Yours obediently,
Yash
Compose an email for my son's teacher, Ms. Alvarez, asking for a meeting about his reading. Say that I am free after 5 pm on weekdays. About 70 words. My name is Peter Dsouza.

Subject: Request for a short meeting

Dear Ms. Alvarez,
I am Peter Dsouza, Arjun's father. I would like to talk to you about his reading and how I can support him at home. Could we meet for a few minutes this week? I am free after 5 pm on any weekday. Please suggest a time that suits you. Thank you for all your help.
Kind regards,
Peter Dsouza
Write an email to my manager asking permission to join an online communication-skills course on Saturdays. About 70 words. I'm Hari.

Subject: Request to join a communication-skills course

Dear Manager,
I would like to join an online communication-skills course that runs on Saturday mornings for six weeks. I believe it will help me write better reports and speak with confidence in meetings. The classes will not affect my work hours, but I wanted your permission before enrolling. May I have your approval?
Thank you for your consideration.
Regards,
Hari
Write a polite email to the neighbour who shares our water tank, asking if we can take turns cleaning it every month. About 75 words. I'm Sudha, from the ground floor.

Subject: Cleaning the shared water tank

Dear Neighbour,
I hope you and your family are well. Since we share the water tank, I wondered if we could take turns to clean it every month. I can arrange the cleaning this time, and you could handle the next. It would keep the water fresh for all of us. Please tell me what you think.
Warm regards,
Sudha

Describe a small railway station at dawn in about 80 words.

The railway station wakes up before the sun. A tea-seller lights his stove, and the first steam rises into the cold air. Pigeons shuffle on the tracks, and a porter yawns beside his trolley. The loudspeaker crackles with a sleepy voice announcing the first train. Passengers huddle in shawls and carry old bags tied with rope. The sky turns pink behind the water tank. When the whistle blows, the whole platform comes alive at once.
Describe a village fair on a winter evening, about 90 words.

The village fair glitters under strings of yellow bulbs. A giant wheel turns slowly, and the children scream with joy as it rises. Women bargain for bangles at small stalls, and the air smells of hot jalebis and roasted corn. A drummer plays near the temple while a magician draws a crowd. Boys throw rings at prizes they will never win, and laugh anyway. Everyone wears woollen caps and warm smiles. When the night grows late, the lights go on shining, and nobody wants to leave.
Describe a neighbourhood bakery in the morning, in about 80 words.

The bakery on our lane opens at six, and the smell of fresh bread reaches the end of the street. Inside, trays of golden buns and soft pav are lined up on the counter. The baker's hands are covered in flour, and he hums as he works. Children press their noses against the glass case and point at the cream rolls. A bell rings with every customer. Soon the shelves are half empty, but the warm smell stays all day.
In around 75 words, describe a mountain lake covered in morning fog.

The lake lies silent under a thick white blanket of fog. You cannot see the other shore, only the dark outlines of pine trees that seem to float in the air. The water is still, like glass. A single duck glides through the mist and leaves a thin ripple behind. Cold air touches your cheeks, and everything sounds soft and far away. Slowly, the sun rises, and the fog lifts like a curtain.
A girl's diary entry about a school picnic to a river, about 80 words, please.

Saturday

Dear Diary,
Today was the best day ever! Our whole class went on a picnic to the river. We played antakshari on the bus, and Mr. Verma sang louder than all of us. I am so sleepy now, but I do not want this day to end.
Diary page, about 90 words, for a boy who has just moved into a hostel away from home.

Sunday night

Dear Diary,
Today my parents left me at the hostel. I waved bravely until their car disappeared, and then I felt a lump in my throat. The room is small, and my roommate Faizan seems friendly. He shared his biscuits with me. The dinner bell rang at eight, and the food was plain but warm. I miss Mummy's cooking and my little sister's noise. I will try to be strong. Tomorrow, I will find the way to my classroom without getting lost.

Friday

Dear Diary,
We lost the final today, 21-18 in the last game. I felt so angry on the court that I threw my racket. Later, I felt ashamed. Our coach said that we played with heart, and that this is just one match. My partner Reema cried, and I hugged her. I think we will practise even harder now. I will not give up. Next year, the cup will be ours.
I need a diary entry, about 80 words, of a child at home alone on a rainy Sunday who finds a way to have fun.

Sunday

Dear Diary,
It rained all day, and I was bored. Papa had gone to the shop, and Mummy was out for work. First, I watched the rain, and then I made a fort from cushions and bedsheets. I read my comics in the fort with a torch. After that, I drew a picture of the rain. It turned out to be a very good Sunday after all. When Mummy came home, she loved my fort.
I want a diary entry of about 90 words by a teenager who spent the day helping her grandmother harvest vegetables at the farm.

Thursday

Dear Diary,
Today I woke up at five and went to the farm with Ajji. The air smelled of wet soil. We picked tomatoes, brinjals and spring onions, and my hands got dirty. Ajji works faster than I do, though she is seventy! She told me stories of her childhood while we filled the baskets. I got a blister on my thumb, but I did not mind. At noon, we ate roti and chutney under a tree. It was the best lunch I have had.
Write a tiny story for children, about 100 words, about a lost baby elephant who finds his way home by following a song.

Bholu, a baby elephant, wandered away from his herd while chasing a butterfly. Soon he was lost deep in the forest, and the trees all looked the same. He felt scared and began to cry. Then he heard a soft song, far away. It was his mother, humming the tune she sang each night. Bholu followed the sound through the bushes and across the stream. At last he saw the herd and ran into his mother's trunk. "Never wander off again," she said, smiling. Bholu promised, and fell asleep to the song.
Write a short story for kids, about 85 words, about a girl who bakes a cake for her mother's birthday but it sinks in the middle.

Kavya wanted to surprise her mother with a cake. She mixed the flour, sugar and eggs carefully and put the cake in the oven. But when she took it out, the middle had sunk into a deep hole. Kavya's eyes filled with tears. Then her little brother had an idea. They filled the hole with whipped cream and strawberries. When Mummy came home, she gasped. "What a special cake!" she said, and hugged them both. Kavya learnt that mistakes can sometimes make things even sweeter.
Write a story, around 85 words, for primary school children about two friends who quarrel over a toy and then solve the problem.

Sameer and Raju both loved the red toy truck. One day, they pulled it so hard that a wheel came off. "You broke it!" cried Sameer. "No, you did!" said Raju. They sat far apart and did not talk. Soon, they felt sad and lonely. Then Raju picked up the wheel and said, "Shall we fix it together?" They found some glue and worked side by side. The truck rolled again, and both boys smiled. After that, they took turns playing with it.
Tell me a short story for children, about 85 words, about a boy who finds a wallet in the school corridor and returns it.

Dev saw a brown wallet lying in the school corridor. He opened it and found some money and a photo of a girl. He thought about keeping it, but then he imagined the owner crying. He took it to his teacher, Mrs. Rao, who announced it in the assembly. A tall boy from Class 9 ran up, looking very relieved. "Thank you!" he said. "It had my sister's photo." Dev felt warm inside, and from that day, everyone in school knew him as honest Dev.
Write a story for children, about 85 words, about a little seed that is tired of waiting underground.

Deep in the soil, a small seed called Sundar waited and waited. "Nothing ever happens down here," he complained to a worm. "Be patient," said the worm. But Sundar was so bored. Then one day, rain came and soaked the earth. Sundar felt something tickling inside him. A tiny green shoot pushed upward, and it broke through the soil. Above, there was sunshine and a blue sky! Sundar stretched and grew into a strong sapling. "So that is what waiting was for," he said happily.
Why should we be kind to stray animals? Give me a paragraph of about 80 words on it.

Stray animals have no homes, and they often go hungry on hot or rainy days. A little kindness can make a big difference to them. We can put out a bowl of fresh water, share a few scraps of food, or simply speak gently. We should never throw stones or tease them. Animals feel hurt and fear just like us. When we treat them with care, we show that we are kind people, too.
Explain in a paragraph, about 80 words, the benefits of learning a musical instrument for young people.

Learning a musical instrument teaches young people many good things. First, it builds patience, because no one plays well on the first day. It also trains the ears and the hands to work together. Playing in a group teaches teamwork and listening. When you finally play a song for your family, the pride you feel is wonderful. Music can also be a quiet friend on a hard day. Whether it is a flute, a guitar or a harmonium, it is worth the practice.
My teacher asked for a paragraph on 'What Makes a Good Neighbour'. Write about 80 words for a 13-year-old.

A good neighbour is someone who is kind and helpful. She says hello with a smile and does not make loud noises late at night. When there is a problem, a good neighbour is the first to help, whether it is a lost cat or a power cut. She shares sweets at festivals and respects other people's privacy. We may not choose our neighbours, but we can choose to be good ones, and that makes the whole street happier.
Please give me a paragraph of around 80 words about why the monsoon is my favourite season.

The monsoon is my favourite season because it changes everything. After the heat of summer, the first rain makes the whole world smell fresh. The trees turn deep green, and the dusty roads shine. I love to sit by the window with a cup of hot tea and watch the water run down the glass. Sometimes I dance in the rain with my friends, and we do not care if we are wet. For me, rain means happiness.
Write a four-line poem about the moon looking over a sleeping town.

The moon looks down on the sleeping town,
She smiles at the roofs as the stars come down.
She guards each window, each lane, each tree,
And whispers, "Goodnight," to you and me.
Write a short rhyme, 4 lines, for children about a heavy school bag.

My school bag is heavy, it has so much to hold,
Two books, a tiffin, and a bottle that's cold.
My shoulders say, "Oh!" and my back says, "Stop!"
I walk like a turtle with a house on top.
Write a simple 4-line poem about autumn leaves falling.

The leaves come down in red and gold,
They dance and twirl, so brave and bold.
They cover the lane with a rustling sound,
A colourful carpet on the ground.
Write a fun six-line poem about a cup of chai on a cold morning.

The kettle sings, the steam comes up,
I hold my warm and happy cup.
Ginger, cardamom, a pinch of cheer,
The cold goes away when chai is near.
One sip, and I smile, so bright,
Chai makes the morning feel just right.
Write a short poem for my best friend about how we always make each other laugh. Around 65 words, rhyming.

We laugh at jokes that no one gets,
We share our snacks and make our bets.
When days are grey, you make them bright,
You help me feel that things are right.
Through all the years and all the fun,
You're the best friend under the sun.
So here's to us, and here's to more,
To all the laughs we have in store!

Describe a sunrise at the beach in about 80 words.

The sky turns pale grey, then soft pink. A thin line of orange appears at the edge of the sea, and slowly the sun rises like a big gold coin. The waves catch the colour and glow. A few fishermen push their boats into the water, while crows and gulls cry overhead. The sand is cool and damp under bare feet. A small crab runs sideways and disappears into a hole. It is a quiet and perfect start to the day.
Describe a school canteen during the lunch break, about 90 words.

At the lunch bell, the canteen explodes with noise. Children rush in and form a long queue at the counter. Plates clatter, and the cook shouts, "Next!" The air smells of hot samosas and sweet tea. At one table, a group of boys argue about last night's match. At another, two girls share a packet of chips and giggle. A teacher walks past, smiling and shaking her head. Within twenty minutes, the tables are empty again, and the cleaners come in to sweep up the crumbs.
Write about 70 words on how a garden looks on the first day of spring.

On the first day of spring, the garden seems to wake up. Tiny buds open on the rose bushes, and new green leaves peek out from the old branches. Bees buzz from flower to flower, and butterflies flutter about. The grass is soft and wet with dew. A robin sings from the fence. The air is fresh and sweet. After the long, cold winter, everything is alive again, and so are we.
Describe a small town library in the afternoon, about 80 words.

In the afternoon, the town library is quiet and cool. Sunlight falls through the tall windows onto long wooden tables. An old man reads the newspaper, and a girl with plaits sits cross-legged on the floor, lost in a picture book. The librarian stamps cards with a soft thump. The ceiling fan creaks as it turns. There is a smell of old paper and polish. Nobody speaks above a whisper, yet the whole room feels full of stories.
Diary time: a student on the last day of school before the summer holidays, in about 75 words.

Friday

Dear Diary,
It is finally the last day of school! We cleaned our desks, returned our library books, and said goodbye to our teachers. Mrs. Nair gave us all a small bookmark. My best friend Lata and I promised to meet at the park every Tuesday. I walked home slowly, because I did not want to leave the school gate. But I am also excited for ice cream, mangoes and long mornings. Summer, here I come!
Write a diary entry, about 75 words, of a girl who made a new friend at the park today after feeling shy.

Wednesday

Dear Diary,
I felt very shy at the park today. All the children were playing, and I stood alone near the slide. Then a girl with a red ribbon came and asked, "Do you want to play with me?" Her name is Sunaina. We played catch, and we climbed the small hill together. She laughs just like a bell! We decided to meet again tomorrow. I am so glad I said yes.
Diary entry, about 90 words, for a boy who got a very low mark on a test and is nervous about telling his parents.

Monday

Dear Diary,
I got a very low mark in maths today. My stomach felt heavy all the way home. I have been rehearsing what to say to Mummy and Papa. I know I did not study enough, and I feel ashamed. But I think it is better to tell them the truth than to hide the paper. Tonight, I will show it to them and ask for help. I hope they will understand. I must try harder next time.
Write about 90 words in diary form for a traveller on a houseboat in Kerala.

Tuesday

Dear Diary,
We are floating slowly on a houseboat in the Kerala backwaters. The water is calm, and green palm trees line the banks. The cook has made fish curry and red rice, and I ate more than I should. A kingfisher dived near our boat this afternoon. In the evening, we saw village women washing clothes at the edge, and children waved at us. I have never felt so peaceful. I wish this trip would last a month.
Please write a diary entry of about 75 words for a girl who had a fun sleepover with her friends.

Saturday

Dear Diary,
Last night, three of my friends slept over at my house. We made popcorn and watched a funny film. Then we told ghost stories in the dark under blankets, and Ritu screamed so loudly that Mummy came running! We giggled until midnight. This morning, we made pancakes, and Aisha burnt hers. Tell a children's story, about 100 words, about a crow who learns to share a piece of bread with a hungry dog.

Kallu the crow found a big piece of bread and flew to a high branch. Below, a thin brown dog was looking up at him, sniffing. "Please, can I have a little?" the dog asked. "No!" said Kallu. "It is mine." He began to eat, but a crumb fell, and then the whole piece slipped down. Kallu was sad and hungry. Then the dog picked it up, broke it in two, and offered Kallu half. Kallu was ashamed. "Thank you," he whispered. From then on, they shared everything they found.
Write a tiny story, about 80 words, for children about a boy who forgets his homework and tells the truth.

Rahul forgot his homework notebook at home. In the morning, his friend Jay whispered, "Say your dog ate it!" Rahul thought about it, but his tummy felt funny. When the teacher asked, he stood up and said, "Ma'am, I forgot my notebook. I am sorry." The class waited. Ma'am smiled. "Thank you for being honest, Rahul. Bring it tomorrow." Rahul felt light as a feather. At home, he finished his work, packed it first in his bag, and went to bed happy.
Write a gentle story for small children, about 85 words, about a girl who is scared of thunder, and her grandmother helps her.

Mira hated thunder. Whenever the sky growled, she hid under her blanket. One stormy night, the thunder was very loud, and she ran to her grandmother's room. "Ajji, I am scared," she whispered. Ajji hugged her and said, "Let's count the seconds after each flash. Thunder is just the sky clapping." They counted together, and each clap felt smaller. Soon, Mira was giggling. "The sky is clapping for the rain!" she said. That night, she slept peacefully, and she was never afraid of thunder again.
Write a short story, around 100 words, for kids about a boy who lights a diya for the first time and learns to be careful.

Arnav was seven, and he wanted to light a diya on Diwali night. "Let me do it, Papa!" he begged. Papa gave him a long matchstick and showed him how to hold it away from his clothes. Arnav's hands shook, but he lit the wick. The little flame danced. "Wow!" he said. Then a breeze came, and his sleeve almost touched it. Papa gently moved him back. "Fire is beautiful, but we must be careful," he said. Arnav nodded. He placed the diya at the door and smiled.
Make up a story for children, about 100 words, about a turtle who wins a race by never giving up.

Tara the turtle wanted to join the forest race, and the animals laughed. "You are too slow," they said. But Tara signed up anyway. At the start, the rabbit and the deer dashed away. Tara walked one step at a time, never stopping. By noon, the rabbit was napping, and the deer was drinking water. Tara kept going, past the hill and the stream. In the evening, she crossed the finish line first, tired and smiling. The animals gasped and then clapped. "You won," said the owl, "because you never gave up."
Can you give me a short paragraph, about 80 words, on why we should say 'thank you' more often?

Saying "thank you" costs nothing, but it means so much. When we thank a person, we show that we notice what she or he did for us. It makes the other person feel respected and happy. A simple thank you to the bus driver, the shopkeeper or the cleaner can brighten their whole day. It also teaches us to be grateful for small things. If we say it every day, kindness will spread, and the world will feel a little warmer.
A paragraph for a nature club newsletter, about 70 words, on why we should save water at home.

Water is precious, and we must use it wisely. A running tap while we brush our teeth wastes many litres. We can close it between uses and fix every leaking pipe. We can collect used water to wash the floor or to water plants. Small habits at home may seem tiny, but together they save a lot. If we save water today, our children will have enough to drink tomorrow.
Write 80 words on how a family dinner without phones feels, for a school essay about family time.

A family dinner without phones feels warm and close. We look at each other's faces instead of our screens. My father tells funny stories from his office, and my little sister explains her drawings with her mouth full. We laugh, we pass the dal and rice, and we really listen. Nobody is in a hurry. When dinner ends, we feel full, not only in the stomach but also in the heart. It is the best part of my day.
Write a four-line poem for children about a little frog who jumps in puddles.

A little green frog went hop, hop, hop,
He jumped in puddles, he would not stop.
Splash! went the water, up to his chin,
And all of his friends said, "Come on in!"
Please write a rhyme of 6 lines for a toddler about brushing teeth before bed.

Brush, brush, brush your teeth,
Up on top and underneath.
Little circles, round and round,
Make a clean and happy sound.
Rinse and spit, and say goodnight,
Sparkly smile, shiny bright!
Could you compose a short poem, 4 to 6 lines, about being homesick when you move to a new city?

The streets are strange, the faces new,
I miss the home I always knew.
The evening lights are bright and loud,
But I feel small inside the crowd.
Still, hope will rise like morning's glow,
And friendly faces I will know.
Write a rhyming poem of four lines about a rainbow after the rain.

The rain has gone, the sky is bright,
A rainbow shines with coloured light.
Red and yellow, green and blue,
A painted bridge in every hue.
I'd like a short poem, about 55 words, thanking teachers, to recite on Teachers' Day.

You teach us letters, you teach us sums,
You wipe our tears when sadness comes.
You show us how to be good and kind,
You plant great dreams within our mind.
Thank you for your patient care,
For all the lessons that you share.
We will remember you each day,
Dear teachers, in every way.
Say thank you to my colleague Prakash for covering my shift when my father was visiting from abroad. About 50 words, please.

Dear Prakash,
Thank you for covering my shift last Friday. Because of you, I could spend the whole day with my father, who had flown in for just a short visit. I will happily return the favour whenever you need it. You are a wonderful colleague.
Warm regards,
Alok
I need to politely remind my flatmate Brinda that she owes me her share of the broadband bill. Around 45 words, no pressure.

Hi Brinda,
Hope your day is going well. This is just a small reminder that the broadband bill is due soon, and I have paid the full amount for this month. Could you send me your share when you get a chance? Thanks a lot, and no hurry today.
Sneha
I promised my friend Zubin I'd help him move and then cancelled. Write a short, honest sorry message, about 55 words.

Hi Zubin,
I am really sorry that I cancelled on moving day. I know you counted on me, and I let you down. I should have told you earlier. Can I come over this weekend and help you unpack and set up your shelves? I want to make it up to you.
Faisal
Our neighbours' daughter Ananya got into medical college. Write them a message of congratulations, about 55 words.

Dear Mr. and Mrs. Iyer,
Heartiest congratulations on Ananya's admission to medical college! We have watched her study so hard, and she truly deserves this. You must be so proud. Please give her our blessings and best wishes. We are sure she will be a wonderful doctor one day.
Warm regards,
The Sinha family
A friend has just returned home from the hospital after a long stay. Write a warm welcome-back message, about 55 words, with no medical advice.

Dear Meghna,
Welcome home! The house must feel so good after all that time away. We missed you so much, and we are very happy to know you are back with your family. Please take all the time you need. We are always here whenever you want a chat or a cup of tea.
Your friends
Congratulate my brother Chirag, who just ran his first ten-kilometre race and finished. Around 50 words, with a bit of humour.

Dear Chirag,
You did it! You actually ran ten kilometres, and you did not stop for samosas on the way. I am so proud of you. Your legs may complain tomorrow, but your medal looks great. Let's celebrate with a lazy Sunday and a big plate of food.
Your sister, Vani
Write a short message for my father who is travelling tonight, wishing him a safe journey. Around 40 words.

Dear Papa,
Wishing you a safe and comfortable journey tonight. Please call us when you reach, and do not forget to eat the sandwiches Mummy packed. We will miss you at home and wait for your stories when you return.
Love,
Tina
Remind my parents to switch off the geyser and gas before they leave for the wedding tomorrow. About 40 words, friendly tone.

Dear Mummy and Papa,
Just a little reminder before you leave for the wedding tomorrow. Please switch off the geyser and the gas, and lock the back door. Have a lovely time, and eat a lot of sweets for me!
Love,
Kunal
I'd like to thank the volunteers who cleaned our beach on Sunday. Write a short post, around 55 words, for our community group.

Dear Volunteers,
A big thank you to everyone who came to clean our beach on Sunday. Together, you collected many bags of waste, and the sand looks beautiful again. Your hard work shows how much one small group can do. We are proud to be part of it.
Beach Care Team
My friend Shalini is turning thirty. Write a funny but warm birthday message, about 45 words.

Dear Shalini,
Happy thirtieth birthday! You are officially old enough to give advice and young enough to ignore it. You have always made our group brighter with your laughter and your terrible singing. May this year be full of cake, adventure and very few Mondays. Love you lots!
Meera
Invite our relatives to a small thread ceremony for my son Aryan, about 55 words. It is next Saturday at 9 am at our house, followed by lunch.

Dear Relatives,
We are happy to invite you to the thread ceremony of our son Aryan. It will take place next Saturday at 9 am at our house, and lunch will follow. We would be deeply grateful for your blessings and your presence. Please bring the whole family and share this special day with us.
Yours lovingly,
Hema and Girish
Plan a short invitation, about 50 words, for my team to a Friday evening tea and snacks in the office to welcome a new teammate, Zainab.

Dear Team,
Please join us this Friday at 5 pm in the office pantry for tea and snacks. We are welcoming our new teammate, Zainab, who joins the design group. Come and say hello, share a laugh, and help her feel at home. Samosas are on the way!
Warm regards,
Jyoti
I'm starting a small book club for friends. Write an invitation about 55 words for the first meeting at my house on Sunday at 4 pm. We will discuss one short story.

Hello book lovers,
I am starting a small book club, and I would love to have you join. Our first meeting is at my house on Sunday at 4 pm. We will talk about one short story, which I will send you tomorrow. There will be tea, biscuits and good conversation. Come as you are, and bring a friend.
Ananya
Invite my neighbours' kids to a free cycling day I am hosting on Saturday morning at 8 in the lane behind the park, around 50 words.

Dear children,
Come and join our Cycling Day this Saturday at 8 in the morning in the lane behind the park. Bring your own bicycle and a helmet. We will have fun races, balance games and some cool water at the end. Your parents are welcome to come and cheer. See you there!
Uncle Rajan
Our colony is holding a Christmas carol evening. Could you draft the invitation, about 55 words? Friday, 7 pm, near the clock tower.

Dear Neighbours,
Come and sing with us at our Christmas Carol Evening this Friday at 7 pm near the clock tower. Bring your voices, your family and a warm jacket. We will have cake, hot chocolate and plenty of joyful music. Everyone is welcome, whether you can sing well or not. Let us fill the lane with cheer!
The Colony Choir
A mobile shop sold me a charger that does not work. Write a polite complaint to the shopkeeper, around 60 words, asking for a replacement. I bought it on Monday. I'm Lakshman.

Dear Sir,
I bought a phone charger from your shop on Monday, and it does not work. I tried it with two different phones, and neither of them charged. I have the bill and the box with me. Could you please replace it or return my money? I would be grateful for your help.
Yours sincerely,
Lakshman

Dear Manager,

I called the front desk twice, but nobody came. Please send housekeeping as soon as possible. I am sure you will take this seriously. Thank you.

Anand Verma
Help me ask my upstairs neighbour, kindly, to stop hanging wet clothes that drip onto my balcony. About 55 words.

Dear Neighbour,

Warm regards,
Madhavi, Flat 3

There is a large pothole on the pavement near the vegetable market on Station Road. Yesterday, an elderly lady almost fell in it. Many shoppers use this path every day, so it could cause an accident. I request you to have it repaired as soon as possible. Thank you for your attention.
Yours sincerely,
A concerned resident

Pallavi

Divya

Gita

Women's Welfare Group

Cultural Group

Seva Group

Station Manager
Describe a busy bus stop in the evening in about 85 words.

At six in the evening, the bus stop is packed. Office workers stand with tired faces and heavy bags, checking their watches. A flower-seller offers jasmine strings, and a boy sells peanuts in paper cones. When a bus arrives, everyone pushes forward at once, and the conductor shouts the stops. A small girl waits by her mother, holding her hand tightly. Horns blare and dust rises. Finally, the bus moves away, and a quiet minute follows before the next crowd arrives.
Describe how a street looks on a winter morning with fog, about 80 words.

The street is wrapped in a soft grey fog. Cars crawl with their lights on, and the streetlamps look like pale moons. People walk with shawls tied over their heads and breath that rises like smoke. A man at the corner warms his hands at a small fire. The milkman's bicycle bell rings somewhere in the mist, but you cannot see him. Everything is slow and muffled, as if the world has been wrapped in cotton.
Describe a flower market just before a festival, in about 90 words.

The flower market is a flood of colour. Heaps of orange marigolds, white jasmine and red roses lie in baskets on the ground. Women thread garlands quickly, their fingers busy and quick. The scent is so strong that it makes you dizzy. Buyers bargain loudly, and sellers shout the price of a metre of flowers. A boy carries a huge sack of petals on his head. Bees buzz around in the morning light. Every stall seems to say that the festival will be beautiful.
Describe my grandfather's armchair and the corner of the house where he sits, in about 90 words. He reads the newspaper there every morning.

In the corner of the front room, beside the window, stands my grandfather's old brown armchair. Its leather is cracked and soft, and the arms are worn from many years of use. Every morning, he sits there with a newspaper and a cup of tea, and the sunlight falls across his glasses. A small table beside him holds his spectacles case and a brass bell. Nobody else sits in the chair. It feels like a quiet throne in our busy home.
I'd like a diary entry, about 75 words, for a shopkeeper at the end of a very slow day with almost no customers.

Wednesday night

Dear Diary,
It was a very slow day. Only five customers came, and two of them just asked for directions. I sat behind the counter and arranged the shelves three times. The rain kept everyone at home. Still, old Mrs. Joshi came in for her bread and chatted with me for half an hour. That was nice. Tomorrow is a new day, and hopefully the sun will bring people back to the shop.
Write the diary entry of an old woman who is happy because her grandchildren visited her for the whole day. About 75 words.

Sunday

Dear Diary,
Today my house was full of noise again, and I loved every minute of it. My grandchildren came in the morning with a bag of mangoes and big hugs. We played carrom, and little Sia beat me twice. I cooked puris and aloo curry, and they finished it all. When they left in the evening, the house became quiet. But my heart is full, and I will sleep with a smile tonight.
A diary entry of about 80 words, please, for a young man who has just finished painting his first big canvas.

Saturday

Dear Diary,
Tonight I put the last stroke on my first big painting. It took me six weeks. It shows our old banyan tree at sunset. I stepped back, and for the first time I felt proud of my work. Of course, the leaves are a bit crooked, and the sky is too orange. But it is mine. I will hang it in my room and show it to my friends tomorrow. I want to paint more.
Diary entry, about 95 words, by a person who feels nervous before the first day of a new job tomorrow.

Sunday night

Dear Diary,
Tomorrow I start my new job, and I cannot sleep. I have ironed my shirt twice and packed my bag three times. What if I forget someone's name? What if I make a mistake in the first hour? Then I tell myself that everyone feels nervous on the first day. I will smile, listen well, and ask questions. I will reach early and take a deep breath at the door. Whatever happens, I will learn something new. Goodnight, diary.
Could you write a diary entry, about 85 words, for a girl on her first aeroplane ride.

Monday

Dear Diary,
Today I flew in an aeroplane for the first time! At the airport, I stared at the big planes outside the glass. When ours began to run, my heart thumped. Then, suddenly, we were in the air, and the houses below looked like tiny toys. I saw the clouds from above, white and fluffy like mountains of cotton. The juice and snacks were also good. I did not want to land. I will fly again someday.
Write a short story for children, about 80 words, about a fisherman who finds a tiny fish in his net and decides to let it go.

Old Raghu cast his net into the sea every morning. One day, among the big fish, he found a tiny silver one. "You are too small to sell," he said. The little fish trembled. Raghu looked at it for a while, then gently lowered it back into the water. "Go and grow," he said. Years later, when his nets stayed empty during a storm, a huge shoal of silver fish swam in. Raghu smiled. He knew the sea remembered kindness.
Please write a funny story, about 100 words, for children about a monkey who steals a hat and gets into trouble.

Bantu the monkey saw a red hat on a cart and grabbed it. He put it on his head and danced happily on a roof. But the hat was too big, and it fell over his eyes. He could not see! He walked straight off the roof and landed in a pile of hay. The hat's owner, a hat seller, laughed. "You look like a little king," he said. Bantu felt silly. He gave the hat back, and the seller gave him a banana in return. Bantu went home happy.
Story for young readers, please, about 100 words, in which two friends get lost in a market and find each other by singing a song.

Asha and Noor were shopping with their grandmother when a crowd pushed them apart. Both girls were lost in the busy market. Asha felt scared, and she tried to call, but her voice was lost in the noise. Then she remembered their favourite song and started to sing it. At the other end of the market, Noor heard the tune and sang back. They followed each other's voices until they met near the sweet shop. They hugged tightly. "Next time, we hold hands," they said, and held them all the way home.
Write a bedtime story, around 100 words, about a little girl who cannot sleep until her father shows her how to count the stars.

Little Riya could not sleep. She tossed and turned, and her pillow felt too warm. Her father came in and said, "Let's go to the window." They looked at the dark sky full of stars. "Let's count them, softly," he said. They began, one, two, three, and soon lost count. Riya laughed quietly. "There are too many!" Her father tucked her in. "Then count them in your dreams," he whispered. Riya closed her eyes and began to count again. Before she reached ten, she was fast asleep.
Give me a story for children, around 85 words, about a baby bird who is afraid to fly from the nest and finds the courage.

Pinky, a baby sparrow, sat at the edge of her nest and looked down. The ground was very far away. "I'll fall," she whispered. Her mother flew nearby and called, "Just spread your wings, dear." Pinky shut her eyes and jumped. For a moment, she dropped, and her tummy tickled. Then the wind caught her tiny wings, and she was flying! She saw the treetops and the sunlit river. "I am flying!" she chirped. Her mother smiled. From that day, Pinky flew every morning without fear.
Write a paragraph, about 80 words, on how video calls help families who live far apart.

Video calls bring families closer when they live far apart. A grandmother in a village can see her grandson's first steps in another city. Parents can watch their children blow out birthday candles on a screen. Festivals no longer feel lonely, because everyone can share the sweets and songs together. Of course, a call is never the same as a hug, but it makes the distance feel smaller. A smiling face on a screen can brighten even a hard day.
I need a paragraph of about 80 words on why home-cooked food tastes special.

Home-cooked food tastes special because it is made with care. The person who cooks knows who likes less salt and who wants an extra chilli. The smell of tadka drifting from the kitchen tells us that someone is thinking of us. We eat together and talk about our day. Even a simple meal of dal and rice feels like a feast when it is made at home. It feeds not only our hunger, but also our hearts.
Put into a paragraph, about 70 words, the pleasure of an evening walk after a busy day.

An evening walk is a gentle reward after a busy day. The sun is soft, and the air feels cooler. You see neighbours chatting, children playing, and birds returning to their trees. Your mind slows down and your worries seem smaller. You can walk alone and think, or with a friend and talk. When you return home, you feel calm and ready for a simple dinner and a good night's sleep.
Write a paragraph of about 70 words about what I like about gardening. I grow tomatoes and roses on my balcony.

I love gardening because it teaches me patience. On my balcony, I grow tomatoes and roses in old tins and pots. Every morning, I water them and look for new buds. When a red tomato finally ripens, I feel so proud. Sometimes the roses bring a butterfly or a bee. Gardening is slow, quiet work, but it makes my days cheerful. A small green corner can bring a big joy.
Write a short poem, six lines, about a river that flows from the mountains to the sea.

From a mountain's snowy crown I start,
I tumble down with a joyful heart.
Through valleys, fields and towns I flow,
Where children splash and grasses grow.
At last I meet the sea so wide,
And rest in her arms at the end of my ride.
Write a four-line lullaby for a baby.

Sleep, my little one, sleep tight,
The moon is up, the stars are bright.
Close your eyes, the day is done,
Dream of sunshine and of fun.
Write a funny four-line poem about a hungry elephant who ate all the bananas.

A hungry elephant, big and grey,
Ate all the bananas in one day.
His tummy rumbled, "Oh, what a shame!
Now there are none, and I'm to blame!"
Write a short rhyme with 4 lines about two friends who play together every evening.

We meet at five, you and me,
We play beneath the mango tree.
We run and jump, we laugh and shout,
Until the stars come peeking out.
Write a simple poem of 4 to 6 lines about feeling proud after finishing something difficult.

I climbed the hill, the path was steep,
My legs were tired, my breath was deep.
But when I stood upon the top,
I smiled so wide I could not stop.
The world looked small, the sky looked free,
And I felt proud of what I could be.
My cousin Meera made me a handmade bookmark with dried flowers for my birthday. Write a thank-you note to her, about 45 words.

With love,
Your cousin

Your sibling

Warm wishes

Your friend

Your friend

Class Teacher

Your friend

Hi everyone,
Let us study for the science exam together! Please come to my house on Thursday at 6 pm. Bring your notebooks and any questions you want to ask. We can test each other and share our best tips. My mother will make some tea and snacks for us. Hope you can join!
We want to invite our cousins to a Raksha Bandhan lunch at our house. Write a warm invitation in about 55 words. Mention that all the sisters will tie rakhis before lunch.

Dear cousins,
Raksha Bandhan is almost here, and we would love to celebrate with you. Please join us for lunch at our house. All the sisters will tie rakhis before we eat, so come a little early. We will have plenty of food and plenty of laughter. It would not feel complete without you!
With love
An online shop sent me school shoes in the wrong size. Write a polite email to the shop, about 70 words, asking to exchange them for the correct size.

Subject: Request to exchange shoes

Dear Sir or Madam,
I ordered a pair of school shoes from your online shop, but the pair that reached me is the wrong size. I have not worn them, and they are still in the box. Could you please tell me how I can exchange them for the correct size? I would be grateful for a reply soon, as school reopens shortly. Thank you for your help.
Yours faithfully
Write a polite request, about 50 words, to our sports teacher to let me borrow the school football for the weekend, because my cousins and I want to practise. I promise to return it on Monday.

Dear Sir,
May I please borrow a school football for this weekend? My cousins and I would like to practise together. I promise to look after it carefully and return it to you on Monday morning. I would be very grateful for your permission. Thank you for your time.
Yours respectfully
The air conditioning was not working during the film we saw at a cinema hall, and the seats were sticky. Write a polite complaint to the manager, about 70 words.

Dear Manager,
We watched a film at your cinema hall recently, and I must share two problems. The air conditioning was not working, so the hall became very hot. The seats were also sticky and uncomfortable. We enjoyed the film, but these things spoiled our evening. I hope you will look into them soon, so that other visitors can feel comfortable.
Yours sincerely
The streetlight in our lane has not worked for two weeks, and it is dark at night. Write a letter, about 65 words, to the municipal office asking them to repair it.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to report that the streetlight in our lane has not worked for two weeks. The lane is very dark at night, and it is hard for children and older people to walk safely. I request you to send someone to repair the light as soon as possible. Thank you for your attention.
Yours faithfully
A laundry shrank my sweater and offered no apology. Write a polite complaint, about 60 words, to the shop owner.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I gave my favourite sweater to your laundry last week. When I collected it, it had shrunk and no longer fits me. When I mentioned this at the counter, nobody apologised. I would like to talk about this problem calmly. Please contact me so that we can find a fair solution.
Yours sincerely
Write an email, about 50 words, to my course coordinator asking when the certificates for last week's workshop will be sent.

Subject: Workshop certificates

Dear Coordinator,
I attended last week's workshop and enjoyed it very much. I wanted to ask when the certificates will be sent to the participants. Could you please let me know the expected date? I need it for my records. Thank you for your help.
Kind regards
Write a short email, about 55 words, to my colleague sharing today's meeting notes and asking her to review them by Thursday.

Subject: Meeting notes for review

Hi,
Please find today's meeting notes attached. Could you read through them and tell me if I have missed anything or written anything wrongly? It would be great if you could review them by Thursday, so that I can send the final version to everyone. Thank you for your help.
Best regards
I need a quotation for 40 chairs for our school function. Write an email, about 60 words, to a furniture vendor asking for the price and delivery time.

Subject: Request for a quotation

Dear Sir or Madam,
We are organising a school function and need 40 chairs. Could you please send me a quotation with the price per chair and the total cost? Please also tell me how soon you can deliver them. We would like to decide this week. Thank you very much.
Yours faithfully
I got into the college I wanted. Write an email, about 80 words, to my old school teacher who always encouraged me, telling her the news and thanking her.

Subject: Good news and thank you

Dear Teacher,
I hope you are well. I am writing to share some happy news: I have got a place in the college I wanted. I still remember how you encouraged me in class when I doubted myself. Your belief in me made a real difference, and I am truly grateful. I will visit the school soon to meet you in person.
With respect and thanks
Email HR, in about 60 words, to ask whether my training session can be moved to the following week, because I will be travelling for a family function.

Subject: Request to change my training date

Dear HR team,
I am scheduled to attend the training session this week, but I will be travelling for a family function. Would it be possible to move my session to the following week? I am happy to join any batch that suits you. Please let me know. Thank you for your understanding.
Regards
Notice wanted, about 50 words: the school lost-property box will be emptied on the last Friday of the month, so students should collect their things before then.

NOTICE
The lost-property box will be emptied on the last Friday of this month. Students who have lost any item, such as a bottle, a jacket or a lunch box, should check the box before that day. Please do not wait until the last day.
School Office
Write a notice, about 45 words, for our housing society's annual general meeting on Sunday at 11 am in the clubhouse. All residents should attend.

NOTICE
The annual general meeting of our housing society will be held this Sunday at 11 am in the clubhouse. All residents are requested to attend, as important matters about the society will be discussed. Please be on time. Your views are valuable.
Secretary
Housing Society
Make a notice, about 45 words, saying the art room will be closed all week while it is being repainted. Classes will use the library instead.

NOTICE
The art room will remain closed all this week while it is being repainted. Art classes will be held in the library instead. Students should carry their drawing books and pencils to the library. Please do not enter the art room until further notice.
Art Department
Our grocery co-op needs a notice, about 40 words, reminding members to bring their own cloth bags, because plastic bags will no longer be given.

NOTICE
From now on, our co-op will no longer give out plastic bags. Members are requested to bring their own cloth bags when they come to shop. This will help keep our streets and drains clean. Thank you for your cooperation.
Management
Describe an auto rickshaw ride through narrow lanes in a busy old city, about 65 words.

The auto rickshaw rattles into the narrow lane, and the driver honks twice at a boy on a bicycle. Shop signs brush past my shoulder, and the smell of frying samosas drifts in. We slow down for a cow resting in the middle of the road, then squeeze past a vegetable cart. Every turn feels like a small adventure. I hold the bar tightly and smile.
Describe a bowl of hot rasam on a rainy day in about 60 words.

Outside, the rain drums on the roof. Inside, a steel bowl of hot rasam sits in front of me. The red-gold soup is thin and fragrant, with curry leaves floating on top. The first sip is sour, spicy and warm all at once. It clears my nose and warms my fingers. I close my eyes, and for a moment the whole grey day feels cosy.
Describe a school playground right after the last bell rings, about 70 words.

The last bell rings, and the doors burst open. Children pour into the playground like water from a tap. Bags are thrown on the grass, and a ball is already flying. Two girls race to the swing, laughing. A teacher calls out a gentle warning to slow down, but nobody listens. The quiet building behind them seems to sigh with relief. The playground is full of noise again.
Describe a lighthouse at dusk, about 70 words.

At dusk the lighthouse stands tall on the rocks, white against a darkening sky. Waves crash at its feet and the wind smells of salt. Slowly, the great lamp at the top begins to turn, sending a long beam across the water. A small fishing boat glides home along that bright path. The lighthouse does not move. It simply watches and guides, night after night.
Describe the view of green fields from a hot-air balloon in about 75 words.

The balloon rises so gently that I hardly feel it leave the ground. Below me, the fields spread out like a patchwork quilt in every shade of green.
