A thin river curls through them, shining in the morning sun. Tiny houses sit among the trees, and a farmer looks up and waves. It is very quiet up here, except for the occasional roar of the burner. I feel light and free.
A diary entry, about 65 words, for a girl on the day she learned to whistle after weeks of trying.

Dear Diary,
Today I finally learned to whistle! I have been trying for weeks, and my lips only made a puff of air. This afternoon I stood by the window, rounded my lips gently and blew softly. A clear little note came out! I ran to show my brother, and he clapped. I felt so proud. Now I want to learn a whole song. Goodnight!
Please write about 70 words in diary form for a boy who lost his first tooth today and feels both excited and a little scared.

Dear Diary,
My first tooth came out today! It was wobbly for days, and while I was eating an apple, it just fell into my hand. I was a little scared when I saw the gap, but also very excited. My sister said the tooth fairy might visit. I put the tooth under my pillow before bed. I keep poking the gap with my tongue. It feels so funny!
Diary time: about 70 words for a girl who finished reading her first big novel and feels sad that it has ended.

Dear Diary,
I finished my first big novel tonight. It had so many pages that I thought I would never reach the end, but I did. Now I feel strangely sad. I spent so many evenings with the characters, and they felt like friends. I closed the book and held it for a minute. I will start another soon, but this one will always be special. Goodnight, Diary.
I need a diary page, about 70 words, for a young woman the night before her sister's wedding, feeling happy and a little emotional.

Dear Diary,
Tomorrow my sister gets married. The house is full of flowers and relatives, and the smell of sweets is everywhere. Tonight we sat on the terrace and talked, just the two of us, like when we were little. I felt happy for her, but I also felt a small ache, because things will change. She squeezed my hand and said nothing. I will remember this night always.
Write a diary entry, about 65 words, from a boy who tried cooking an omelette for the first time and burnt the first one.

Dear Diary,
Today I made an omelette by myself for the first time. The first one burnt black on the bottom, and the whole kitchen smelled of smoke. I was ready to quit, but Mother said everyone burns the first one. I lowered the flame and tried again. The second omelette was golden and soft. I ate it proudly. Next time, I will not forget the salt!
Write a story of about 100 words about a girl, her mango tree and a squirrel who keeps taking the fruit. The ending must be that she learns to share.

Nisha watched her mango tree all summer. When the first fruit turned yellow, a squirrel snatched it and ran. The next day, it took another. Nisha was cross and made a scarecrow, but the squirrel simply sat on its hat. One evening she found the squirrel sitting on a branch, nibbling happily, with its tiny face covered in juice. Nisha laughed. The tree had plenty of fruit. From then on, she picked what she needed and left a few on the lowest branch for her small friend.
Write a story, about 90 words, about a boy whose kite string snaps, and a stranger helps him get the kite back. End with the boy thanking him.

Imran's kite soared high above the rooftops until the string snapped. The kite floated away and caught on a tall tree near the market. Imran stood below, sad and helpless. A stranger carrying a bag of vegetables stopped and looked up. He put down his bag, found a long bamboo pole from a nearby shop and gently lifted the kite from the branches. Imran took it with both hands. "Thank you so much!" he said, grinning. The stranger smiled and went on his way.
Write a gentle story, about 100 words, about a shopkeeper who finds a customer's forgotten umbrella and walks through the rain to return it. End happily.

It rained hard one afternoon, and a woman left her umbrella behind at Mr. Rao's small stationery shop. He noticed it only after she had gone. Mr. Rao looked at the rain, then picked up the umbrella and locked the door. He did not know where she lived, but he remembered she had mentioned the blue house near the temple. He walked there and knocked. The woman opened the door, surprised, and then smiled widely. "You walked all this way for me?" she said. They both laughed and shared tea.
Tell a fable, about 85 words, about a fox who tries to steal a drum, but is surprised by the sound. The fox must learn a lesson at the end.

A hungry fox found a big drum under a tree while the villagers slept. "I will carry it away," he thought, and he tiptoed closer. But his paw hit the drum, and it went BOOM! The fox jumped in fright. Lamps lit up, and the villagers ran out shouting. He dropped the drum and fled into the forest. Panting, he learned that stealing never stays quiet, and that it is better to ask than to take.
Write a short story, about 100 words, about a girl with a magic pencil who draws a bridge so that a line of ants can cross a puddle. Keep it sweet.

Mina found a pencil that glowed softly when she held it. She drew a smiley sun, and warmth filled the room. Then she noticed a line of ants stopped at a big puddle in the yard. They could not cross. Mina knelt down and drew a small bridge from one side to the other. The lines shimmered and became real wood. One by one, the ants marched across, as if saying thank you. Mina smiled and put the pencil away, happy to have helped in such a tiny way.
Write a paragraph of about 70 words on why a regular morning routine helps students start the day well, for a school magazine.

A regular morning routine helps students begin the day calmly. When you wake up, wash and eat at the same time each day, you stop rushing and forgetting things. You have time to pack your bag and enjoy your breakfast. A calm start makes it easier to listen in class and to feel confident. Small habits like these cost nothing, yet they make the whole day easier. Try it for a week and see.
For a school debate, write about 80 words on why walking to school is better than going by car.

Walking to school has many advantages. First, it is good exercise, and it wakes up the body before class. Second, it gives us time to chat with friends or simply enjoy the fresh air. Third, fewer cars mean less smoke and noise near the school gate. Finally, children who walk learn to notice their neighbourhood and its people. A walk of even a few minutes can make the school day start with a smile. That is why walking is the better choice.
Write a paragraph, about 75 words, on why volunteers are important to a community. Make it suitable for a notice board.

Volunteers are the quiet helpers of every community. They clean streets, teach children, help older people and organise events, without asking for payment. When people give a little of their time, big things become possible. Volunteering also brings neighbours together and builds friendships. If you have a free hour, please think about joining us. Every pair of hands matters, and every small effort makes our neighbourhood a kinder, better place for everyone.
Write a four-line rhyme for children about a school bell that rings too early on a sleepy morning.

The school bell rang, ding-dong, so loud,
It woke me from my cosy cloud.
I yawned and stretched, and rubbed my eyes,
Then rushed to class in sleepy surprise.
Write a short poem, four lines, about a train that runs through the night.

The train goes rolling through the night,
Its windows glow with golden light.
The wheels go clickety-clack, clickety-clack,
And rock me softly down the track.
Write a six-line rhyme for kids about an umbrella that wants to go out in the sunshine.

My umbrella sat beside the door
And sighed, "I'm tired of the pour.
Each time I'm used, the sky is grey;
I'd love a bright and sunny day."
So out we went in morning light,
And it twirled happily, shining bright.
My uncle drove us to the airport at 4 in the morning. Could you write a thank-you note to him, about 50 words?

Dear Uncle,
Thank you for driving us to the airport so early this morning. It was still dark, and I know you gave up your sleep for us. We reached in good time and felt calm because of you. I am truly grateful for your help and your kindness.
With love
I accidentally broke Grandma's steel tumbler while washing up. Please write a short sorry note, about 50 words, that I can leave on the kitchen table.

Dear Grandma,
I am very sorry that I broke your steel tumbler while washing up. I know you have used it for many years. It slipped from my wet hands. Please do not be upset with me. I will wash up more carefully from now on.
Your grandchild
Sana just won our school spelling bee. Write a congratulations message for her, about 45 words.

Dear Sana,
Congratulations on winning the school spelling bee! You stayed so calm on the stage, and you spelled every word correctly. All of us in the class are cheering for you. You have worked hard and you deserve this win. Well done!
Your classmate
Our local tailor altered my sister's wedding blouse overnight when it did not fit. Write a thank-you note to him, about 45 words.

Dear Sir,
Thank you for altering my sister's wedding blouse overnight. It fits perfectly now, and she is very happy. You worked late to help us, and we will never forget it. The whole family is grateful for your skill and your kindness.
With thanks
Remind my flatmate that the wifi bill has to be paid by the 5th. Keep it friendly and short, about 35 words.

Hi,
Just a friendly reminder that the wifi bill has to be paid by the 5th. Could you please send your share before then? Thanks a lot! Let me know if you need anything from me.
Cheers
The night security guard waited at the gate with an umbrella for me when I came home late in the rain. Help me write a thank-you note to him, about 50 words.

Dear Guard,
Thank you for waiting at the gate with an umbrella when I came home late in the rain. It was a small act, but it made me feel cared for. I am grateful for the way you look after our building every night. Please take care of yourself too.
Regards
I laughed at my friend Sunita's new haircut and she looked hurt. Write a sincere apology message, about 50 words.

Dear Sunita,
I am sorry for laughing at your new haircut. It was rude, and I saw that it hurt you. I did not mean to hurt you, but I should have thought before I spoke. The haircut actually suits you. Please forgive me, and let me buy you a coffee to say sorry.
Your friend
My mother has just finished her college degree through evening classes after many years. Write a proud congratulations message for her, about 55 words.

Dear Mother,
Congratulations on finishing your degree! You studied in the evenings after a full day of work at home, and you never gave up. You have shown me that it is never too late to learn. I am so proud of you. We will celebrate together this weekend. I love you very much.
Your child
Our school library wants a short reminder for students, about 40 words, that all borrowed books must be returned before the exams begin.

Dear students,
This is a reminder that all books borrowed from the library must be returned before the exams begin. Please check your bags and shelves at home. Returning books on time helps other students who need them. Thank you for your cooperation.
Librarian
A colleague gave me a small potted plant for my new desk. Write a thank-you message, about 40 words.

Dear colleague,
Thank you for the lovely plant. It brightens up my new desk and makes the space feel like my own. It was a very kind gesture. I promise to water it regularly and keep it healthy!
Best wishes
Please help me invite my family to my graduation ceremony on Saturday at 10 am in the college auditorium. About 50 words.

Dear family,
I am happy to tell you that I will graduate this Saturday at 10 am in the college auditorium. It would mean the world to me if you could all come and share this special day. Please arrive a little early to find good seats. I look forward to seeing you there.
With love
Invite my colleagues to a Sunday morning trek, starting at 6 am from the office car park. Mention that they should wear sturdy shoes. About 50 words.

Hello team,
Let us start our Sunday with a trek! We will leave from the office car park at 6 am sharp. Please wear sturdy shoes and carry some water. It will be a fun way to spend time together outside work. Do join us if you can, and bring along a friend.
Regards
We are hosting an open-mic evening for students in the school hall next Friday at 5 pm. Draft an invitation, about 55 words, for students of all classes.

Open-mic evening for all students!
Do you sing, dance, recite or tell jokes? Come and perform in the school hall next Friday at 5 pm. Students of all classes are welcome to take part or simply cheer from the audience. Put your name down with your class teacher if you wish to perform. Come and enjoy a happy evening.
A potter in our neighbourhood is holding a clay workshop for children on Sunday at 3 pm. Write an invitation for parents, about 55 words.

Dear Parents,
Your child is invited to a clay workshop this Sunday at 3 pm. A local potter will show the children how to shape small bowls and animals with their hands. They will take their creations home once they dry. It will be a messy and happy afternoon. Please bring an old shirt for your child.
Grandparents' Day is on Friday at our school. Write an invitation to our grandparents, about 50 words, inviting them for a morning of songs and tea.

Dear Grandparents,
We warmly invite you to Grandparents' Day at our school on Friday. We will sing songs, show you our classrooms and serve you tea. It is our chance to say thank you for all your love and care. Please come and spend the morning with us. We cannot wait to see you!
Your grandchildren
I sprained my wrist and cannot play in PT class this week. Write a polite request, about 50 words, to my class teacher asking if I can sit out.

Dear Teacher,
I sprained my wrist yesterday and cannot take part in PT class this week. May I please sit out during the period and watch instead? I will join the activities again when my wrist feels better. Thank you for understanding.
Yours obediently
My suitcase arrived two days after my flight landed. Write a polite complaint to the airline, about 70 words, asking them to explain and to make sure it does not happen again.

Dear Sir or Madam,
My suitcase arrived two days after my flight landed. I had to manage without my clothes and other things during that time. I would like to understand why this delay happened. Please look into the matter and reply to me with an explanation. I also request you to take steps so that such delays do not happen to other passengers.
Yours faithfully
The shower at our gym has had no hot water for a week. Write a polite complaint, about 55 words, to the gym manager.

Dear Manager,
I have been a member of your gym for some time and I enjoy my workouts. However, the shower has had no hot water for a week now. This makes it uncomfortable to use, especially in the early morning. I would be grateful if you could look into this and repair it soon.
Yours sincerely
Our library has very few novels for teenagers. Write a polite request to the head librarian, about 60 words, asking if more could be bought.

Dear Librarian,
I enjoy borrowing books from our library, but I have noticed that there are very few novels for teenagers. I read them quickly and then have little left to choose from. May I respectfully request you to buy some more? I think many of my friends would use them too. Thank you for considering this.
Yours sincerely
I bought a storybook from a bookshop and it has six pages missing. Please write a polite complaint, about 60 words, asking for a replacement.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I bought a storybook from your shop recently, and when I started reading it, I found that six pages were missing. I was disappointed, because it was a gift for a child. I have kept the bill. Could you please replace the book with a complete copy? Thank you for your help.
Yours faithfully
Write an email to a pen-friend abroad describing my school day, in about 70 words. I start at 8 am, love lunch break and my favourite subject is geography.

Subject: My school day

Dear friend,
My school day starts at 8 am, when I take the bus with my neighbours. The morning classes go quickly, but I look forward to lunch break, when we share food and play outside. My favourite subject is geography, because I love maps and faraway places. In the evening, I do my homework and read. Tell me about your day too!
Best wishes
I finished the quarterly report a day early. Write a short email to my manager letting her know, in about 50 words, and offering to help with anything else.

Subject: Report completed

Dear Manager,
I am pleased to let you know that the quarterly report is ready and I finished it a day early. I have attached it for your review. If there is anything else you would like me to help with, please tell me.
Regards
I'm a parent, and I'd like an email to a cricket coach asking for the dates of the next trial for under-14 players, in about 55 words. It is for my son.

Subject: Under-14 trial dates

Dear Coach,
I am writing as the parent of a boy who is keen to try out for your under-14 team. Could you please tell me the dates and the time of the next trial? Please also let me know what he should bring. Thank you for your time and guidance.
Yours sincerely
Compose an email to the school office asking for a bonafide certificate, in about 60 words. I am a Class 11 student and need it for a scholarship form.

Subject: Request for a bonafide certificate

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am a student of Class 11 and I need a bonafide certificate to complete a scholarship form. Could you please tell me how I can apply for it and how long it will take? I will collect it from the office in person. Thank you for your help.
Yours faithfully
We have a leaking pipe in the kitchen. Draft an email to a plumber, around 45 words, asking if he can visit on Saturday morning.

Subject: Request for a visit

Dear Sir,
There is a leaking pipe in our kitchen, and we would like it repaired. Could you please visit on Saturday morning? Kindly let me know if that time suits you and what it will cost. Thank you.
Regards
Announce a parent-teacher meeting on Saturday from 10 am to 1 pm. In a notice of about 45 words, ask parents to meet class teachers in their own classrooms.

NOTICE
A parent-teacher meeting will be held this Saturday from 10 am to 1 pm. Parents are requested to meet the class teachers in their own classrooms. Please bring your child's school diary. We look forward to a useful discussion about every child's progress.
Principal
Write a notice, around 40 words, that the bicycle parking area behind our apartment block has moved next to the main gate.

NOTICE
The bicycle parking area behind our apartment block has been moved next to the main gate. Residents are requested to park their cycles in the new place from now on. Please do not leave cycles near the old area. Thank you.
Society Office
We need a notice for Annual Day rehearsals: every day this week after school in the hall, for all students in the dance group. About 45 words, please.

NOTICE
Rehearsals for Annual Day will be held every day this week after school in the hall. All students in the dance group must attend. Please wear comfortable clothes and bring water. Students who cannot attend should inform the dance teacher in advance.
Cultural Committee
Put a short notice on the school gate saying a set of house keys was found near it and can be claimed at the office. About 35 words.

NOTICE
A set of house keys was found near the school gate this morning. The owner may collect them from the school office. Please describe the keys to the office staff when you come to claim them.
School Office
Describe my grandmother's old sewing machine as it hums in a corner of the room, about 70 words.

In the corner of the room sits my grandmother's old sewing machine. Its black body is worn smooth from years of use, and its golden letters have faded. When she presses the pedal, it hums and clatters, and the needle dances up and down. Bits of colourful cloth pile up beside it. She has stitched many clothes on this machine, and each one carries a little of her patience.
Describe the school bus at 7 in the morning, in about 60 words.

The yellow school bus rolls up at 7 in the morning, and the doors fold open with a squeak. Sleepy children climb in with heavy bags. Someone is eating a roll, and two friends are whispering a secret. The driver greets everyone with a smile. The seats fill up, the engine hums, and the bus moves on, full of yawns and early chatter.
Write about 55 words describing a sugarcane juice stall on a hot afternoon.

At the corner, a man feeds long sticks of sugarcane into a clanking machine. Golden juice flows into a tall glass, with ice and a squeeze of lime. The queue of thirsty people grows longer under the hot sun. I take a glass and drink it in one go. It is sweet and cool, and the heat melts away.
Describe the view from the top of a mountain after a hard climb, in about 70 words.

My legs ache and my breath is short, but I have finally reached the top. The whole world lies below me, with tiny villages, silver rivers and rows of misty hills. The wind is cold and fresh, and the sky seems very close. I sit on a rock and drink some water. All the tiredness is gone, replaced by a wide, happy feeling that I cannot put into words.
Describe a fruit seller's cart at midday in the market, about 60 words.

The fruit seller's cart is a rainbow on wheels. Red apples are stacked in neat pyramids, and bananas hang like yellow bunting. Oranges, guavas and grapes crowd together, and the smell of ripe mangoes drifts across the lane. The seller calls out his prices in a singsong voice. A woman presses a papaya gently, smiles and says she will take two.
I'd like about 70 words of diary writing from a girl after her school's Annual Day dance, when she forgot a step but kept going.

Dear Diary,
Tonight was our Annual Day dance. My heart was thumping as the curtain rose. In the middle, I forgot a step and my mind went blank. But I kept smiling and followed the girl next to me. Nobody noticed, and the audience clapped loudly at the end. Mother hugged me and said I was brave. I felt so relieved and proud!
Diary entry for a boy on the day his family brought home a puppy, about 70 words.

Dear Diary,
We brought a puppy home today! He is small and brown, with big floppy ears. At first he hid under the sofa, but soon he came out to sniff my shoes. He chewed my slipper and then fell asleep in my lap. I felt so happy that my chest almost hurt. I think we will be best friends. I must think of a good name for him.
Give me a diary page of about 70 words about a day in my grandparents' village, where I ate fresh guavas and chased chickens.

Dear Diary,
Today I spent the whole day in my grandparents' village. I climbed the guava tree and ate the fresh fruit, with its sweet pink insides. Then I chased the chickens around the yard until they scattered, squawking. My grandmother laughed and told me to stop. In the evening, we sat outside and watched the stars. The city seems so far away. I wish I could stay longer.
Pretend you're a ten-year-old who fell off a bicycle today. Write the diary entry, about 65 words, showing that the child was brave and tried again.

Dear Diary,
Today I fell off my bicycle and scraped my knee. It stung, and I almost cried. For a moment I wanted to put the bicycle away and never ride it again. But my father said I could try again, and I did. I wobbled, but this time I stayed on. My knee still hurts, but I feel brave. Tomorrow I will ride farther.
A girl helped a lost child find his parents at a village fair. Write her diary entry for that evening, about 70 words.

Dear Diary,
Today at the village fair, I saw a little boy standing alone and crying. I asked him his name and held his hand. We walked around the fair and I asked people if they knew his parents. After a while, a worried woman ran towards us and hugged him tightly. She thanked me again and again. I felt happy that I had helped. I hope he is safe tonight.
Tell a story of about 90 words about a girl who loses a glove in the snow. It must end with a hedgehog using it as a bed.

Asha ran across the snowy field, laughing, until she noticed that one of her red gloves was gone. She looked behind every tree and under every bush, but found nothing. Sadly, she went home with one cold hand. Weeks later, when the snow melted, she walked the same path and saw something red under a hedge. The glove was lying there, and inside it a small hedgehog was curled up, fast asleep. Asha smiled and left it as a bed.
Write a story of about 85 words about a boy who builds a robot from junk. At the end, the robot must help him water the garden.

Tarun collected old tins, wires and bottle caps from the junk shop. For weeks he worked in the garage, twisting wires and fixing bolts. Finally, a small robot stood on its square legs. It had two bottle-cap eyes and a funnel for a mouth. Tarun pressed a button, and the robot let out a whirr. It rolled forward on its wheels. The next morning, Tarun handed it a small watering can. The robot gently watered each plant in the garden, row by row, while he watched proudly.
I'd like a story, about 90 words, about a baker who notices a hungry cat outside his shop every night. End with them becoming friends.

Every night, when the baker locked up his shop, he saw a thin cat watching from the corner. At first he chased it away. But one cold evening the cat looked so hungry that the baker felt ashamed. He took a small piece of leftover bread and a saucer of milk and put them by the door. The cat ate slowly and looked up at him. The next evening, it was waiting. Soon it was sleeping beside the warm oven each night, purring contentedly.
Please write a story, about 100 words, about two neighbours who built a wall between their houses and then made a little door in it.

Two neighbours quarrelled over a mango tree, and one of them built a high wall between their houses. For months they did not speak. One day a ball from one garden flew over the wall and landed in the other. The boy next door knocked on the wall, calling for his ball. Nobody answered. His father felt sorry and took a small hammer. By evening there was a little wooden door in the wall. The other neighbour came through it with the ball and a mango. They both laughed, and shared the fruit.
Make up a story, about 80 words, about a smooth grey stone in a stream that dreams of seeing the sea, and a river that finally carries it there.

A smooth grey stone lay in a stream and listened to the water. "Where do you go?" it asked. "To the sea," said the water. The stone sighed. "I wish I could see it." Each day the stream flowed, and each day the stone slipped a little farther. After many seasons, a big monsoon flood lifted the stone and carried it all the way down the river. At last it rolled onto soft sand and heard the great waves. "It is wonderful!" it said.
Write a paragraph for a school newsletter about 70 words long on why we should save water every day, with easy tips like closing the tap while brushing.

Water is precious, and saving it begins with small daily habits. Close the tap while you brush your teeth. Take shorter showers, and use a bucket for washing the bicycle. Fix any dripping tap at home as soon as you can. If we all do these little things, we save thousands of litres in a year. Tomorrow's children will thank us for taking care of water today.
Why does teamwork matter in sport? Write a paragraph for my school magazine, about 75 words.

Teamwork matters in sport because no player can win alone. In a team, each person has a job, and the game goes well only when everyone does it. Players learn to trust one another, pass the ball and support a friend who has made a mistake. A team that works together can beat a team of stars. Teamwork also teaches us to share joy in winning and lessons in losing.
Write 65 words in a paragraph about why neat handwriting still matters, for a class essay.

Neat handwriting still matters, even in a time of keyboards. When writing is clear, others can read it easily, and mistakes are fewer. Taking time to form each letter well also helps us slow down and think. Teachers can mark neat work faster, and notes are easier to revise later. Good handwriting is a small gift to your future self. A little practice each day can improve it.
Write a four-line rhyme for children about a bus that is always late.

The bus is late, the bus is late,
We stand and wait beside the gate.
It finally comes, with a honk and a sigh,
And off we go, as the clouds float by.
Four lines of poetry, please, about the stars coming out one by one at night.

The sun slips down behind the hill,
The world grows quiet, calm and still.
One tiny star, then two, then three,
Are shining bright for you and me.
Write a six-line poem for kids about a pair of red rain boots that love puddles.

My little boots are bright and red,
They splash through puddles, so I said,
"Let's jump in every pool we see,
As deep and wide as it can be!"
My boots cheer loudly, splish and splash,
And off we go in a happy dash.
My grandmother stitched the broken strap of my school bag by hand. Please help me write a thank-you note to her, about 50 words.

Dear Grandmother,
Thank you for stitching the strap of my school bag. It looks as strong as a new one, and your neat stitches make it special. I was worried I would need a new bag, but you saved me. I love you, and I will carry it with pride.
Your grandchild
I used my roommate's phone charger without asking and left it at college. Write a short, sincere sorry message to her, about 50 words.

Hi,
I am sorry that I took your phone charger without asking, and I am even sorrier that I left it at college. I should have asked first. I will bring it back tomorrow. Please tell me if there is anything else I can do to make up for it.
Your roommate
My friend Dev just got his first job. Write him a happy congratulations message, about 45 words.

Dear Dev,
Congratulations on your first job! You worked so hard for this, and I am delighted that it has paid off. I am sure you will do very well. Let us celebrate soon, and the first round is on you! Well done, my friend.
Cheers
Our teammate twisted his knee during practice. Write a get-well message from the team, about 45 words, without any advice about treatment.

Hi teammate,
We were sorry to see you hurt at practice, and we miss you on the field already. Take all the time you need to rest. We are thinking of you and looking forward to seeing you back. Get well soon!
The team
Write a reminder note, about 50 words, for my father to take his spectacles and train ticket when he leaves for the railway station tomorrow.

Dear Papa,
A small reminder for tomorrow: please take your spectacles and your train ticket before you leave for the railway station. Keep them together in your front pocket so that you do not forget. Have a safe and pleasant journey, and call us when you reach.
With love
An electrician came to fix our wiring on a public holiday. Write a thank-you note to him, about 45 words.

Dear Sir,
Thank you for coming to fix our wiring on a public holiday. You gave up your day off, and we are very grateful. The lights are working again, and the house feels safe. Your quick, careful work made a big difference to us.
Regards
We played loud music at my party last night and probably kept the neighbours awake. Write a sorry note to them, about 55 words.

Dear Neighbours,
We are sorry for the loud music at our party last night. We realise it must have kept you awake, and we should have kept the volume lower and ended earlier. Thank you for being patient with us. We will be more careful next time. Please let us know if anything like this bothers you again.
Warm regards
Our school choir won the inter-school competition. Write a congratulations message from the principal to the choir, about 50 words.

Dear choir members,
Congratulations on winning the inter-school competition! Your voices were lovely, and your discipline showed every day in practice. You have made the whole school proud. Please thank your music teacher, who guided you with so much care. Enjoy this win, and keep singing.
Principal
Remind all parents in my class that the winter uniform starts from Monday. Keep it polite and about 35 words.

Dear Parents,
This is a gentle reminder that the winter uniform will be worn from Monday. Kindly make sure your child comes to school in the full winter uniform, including the sweater. Thank you for your cooperation.
Class Teacher
I stayed with a host family for a week during a student exchange. Write them a thank-you note, about 60 words.

Dear host family,
Thank you for welcoming me into your home for a whole week. I loved the meals we shared, the evening walks and the stories you told me. You made me feel like one of the family from the first day. I will always remember your kindness. I hope you can visit me one day, and I can host you.
Gratefully
My mother is retiring after many years of teaching. Write an invitation to a small tea party at our home in her honour, on Sunday at 4 pm. About 50 words.

Dear friends,
After many years of teaching, my mother is retiring, and we would like to honour her with a small tea party at our home. Please join us this Sunday at 4 pm. Your presence will make her feel very special. Come and share your memories and a cup of tea with her.
Warm regards
I help at the neighbourhood library. Write an invitation, about 45 words, for a children's storytelling hour on Saturday at 11 am.

Calling all young readers!
Our neighbourhood library invites you to a storytelling hour this Saturday at 11 am. Come and listen to tales of animals, kings and brave children. Parents are welcome to sit with their little ones. Bring a friend and a cushion, and enjoy a happy morning.
Invite my friends to a stargazing night on our rooftop this Friday after dinner. About 45 words, and tell them to bring a blanket.

Hello friends,
Come and watch the stars with me on our rooftop this Friday after dinner! The sky is clear and the stars are bright. Please bring a blanket to sit on. We will look for patterns in the sky and share stories. See you there!
Our class is holding a bake sale at school next Wednesday to raise money for the library. Write an invitation, about 50 words, to the whole school.

Come to our bake sale!
Our class invites everyone to a bake sale at school next Wednesday. We have cakes, biscuits and many other homemade treats. All the money we raise will be used to buy new books for the library. Please come with your friends and a good appetite. Every bite helps a reader!
My desk chair at the office is broken and hurts my back. Write a polite request to the office administrator, about 55 words, asking for a replacement.

Dear Sir or Madam,
The chair at my desk is broken and has become uncomfortable to sit on for long hours. I request you to kindly arrange a replacement chair for me. I would be very grateful for your help. Please let me know if you need to see the chair. Thank you for your time.
Regards
A tuition centre changed my son's class timing without telling us, and he missed the lesson. Write a polite complaint to the centre, about 60 words.

Dear Sir or Madam,
The timing of my son's class was changed, but nobody informed us, so he missed the lesson. This is upsetting for both of us. I understand that schedules can change, but I request you to send a message to parents when it does. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.
Yours sincerely
Garbage keeps getting left on the stairs of our apartment block. Write a polite complaint to the apartment manager, about 55 words, asking him to take action.

Dear Manager,
I am writing to bring a problem to your notice. Garbage bags are often left on the stairs of our building, and they smell bad and attract flies. Could you please remind residents to use the bins and ask the cleaning staff to check the stairs every day? Thank you for your attention.
Yours sincerely
My maths teacher added my marks wrongly on the answer sheet. Write a polite request, about 50 words, asking him to check the total.

Dear Sir,
I have looked carefully at my maths answer sheet, and I think the marks on the last page may have been added wrongly. May I request you to please check the total again? I am sorry to trouble you. Thank you very much for your time and help.
Yours respectfully
Our travel agent promised a room with a sea view, but we got a room facing a car park. Write a polite complaint, about 65 words, asking for a refund of the difference.

Dear Sir or Madam,
You promised us a room with a sea view for our holiday, but the room we were given faced the car park. We were disappointed, as this was the main reason we chose that hotel. I request you to look into the matter and refund the difference in the price. I look forward to your reply.
Yours sincerely
I'm a teacher. Compose an email to a museum asking about visiting hours and group rates for a school group, in about 60 words.

Subject: Visit by a school group

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am a teacher and would like to bring a group of students to your museum. Could you please tell me your visiting hours and whether there are special rates for school groups? We would also appreciate it if you could say how to book a guided tour. Thank you.
Yours faithfully
Please draft an email asking a colleague to cover a meeting for me on Tuesday afternoon because I have to visit a bank, in about 55 words.

Subject: Can you cover Tuesday's meeting?

Hi,
I have to visit the bank on Tuesday afternoon and cannot attend the meeting. Would you be able to cover it for me? I can send you the agenda and my notes beforehand. I would be happy to return the favour. Thank you so much.
Best regards
I have to quit the school hockey team until my exams are over. Write an email to the coach, about 70 words, that is respectful and says I hope to rejoin.

Subject: Leaving the team for now

Dear Coach,
I am writing to say that I must take a break from the hockey team until my exams are over. I have enjoyed every practice, and I am sorry to leave. I need to give my studies full attention at this time. I hope I can rejoin the team afterwards. Thank you for all your guidance.
Yours sincerely
We want our school sports day to have a chief guest. Write an invitation email, about 70 words, from the principal to a retired athlete who is not named.

Subject: Invitation to our sports day

Dear Sir or Madam,
On behalf of our school, I would like to invite you to be the chief guest at our annual sports day. Your achievements in sport inspire our students greatly. We would be honoured if you could join us, address the children and give away the prizes. Please let me know if you can accept. We hope to see you.
Yours sincerely
Principal
The community swimming pool will be shut next Monday for cleaning. Make a notice of about 40 words for the notice board.

NOTICE
The community swimming pool will remain closed next Monday for cleaning. It will reopen once the cleaning is done. Members are requested to plan their swimming accordingly. We regret any inconvenience this may cause.
Pool Management
Please create a notice, about 50 words, saying that second-hand school uniforms will be sold at low prices in the school hall on Friday after class.

NOTICE
Second-hand school uniforms will be sold at low prices in the school hall on Friday after class. Parents who wish to buy a uniform for their child are welcome to visit. Parents with uniforms their children have outgrown may donate them to the office before Friday.
School Office
Draft a notice, around 45 words, saying that the water tank on our building's roof will be cleaned on Sunday and the water may be muddy that evening.

NOTICE
The water tank on the roof of our building will be cleaned this Sunday. The water may look muddy that evening, so please let it run for a few minutes before use. Please store enough water beforehand. We apologise for the inconvenience.
Society Management
Write a notice, about 35 words, reminding residents that the terrace is closed after 9 pm for the sake of those who are sleeping.

NOTICE
Residents are reminded that the terrace is closed after 9 pm, so that those who are sleeping are not disturbed. Please keep to this rule. Thank you for being considerate.
Society Office
Describe a tailor's shop in a busy market in about 80 words.

The tailor's shop is small and crowded. Rolls of colourful cloth lean against the walls, and a tape measure hangs around the tailor's neck. His sewing machine whirs steadily as he guides a bright green fabric through it. Customers wait on a wooden bench, flipping through old fashion pictures. Threads and buttons lie scattered on the floor, and the air smells of fresh cotton. Every few minutes the tailor looks up, smiles and says, "Almost ready."
Describe a school corridor during exams, in about 60 words.

The corridor is quiet during the exams. The usual shouting and running have stopped. Behind each classroom door, pens scratch on paper. A teacher walks slowly with soft footsteps, and a fan creaks overhead. Outside, a nervous student waits for a late friend, whispering the last answers to himself. The silence feels heavy and full of thinking, until the bell finally rings.
Describe a courtyard in an old house with a tulsi plant in the middle, about 70 words.

In the middle of the courtyard stands a tulsi plant on a small stone platform. Its leaves are green and sweet-smelling, and a little lamp sits at its base. Morning light slants through the open sky above. Pigeons walk along the edge of the roof, and the floor is cool under bare feet. My grandmother waters the plant every morning, and the whole house feels peaceful.
Describe the sunrise over paddy fields in the countryside, in about 60 words.

The sky turns pink and gold over the paddy fields. Mist rests on the green rows, and drops of dew shine on every blade. A farmer walks along the narrow mud path with a tool over his shoulder, and a white egret lifts off from the water. The air is cool and smells of wet earth. The day begins slowly and gently.
Describe sitting around a campfire at night with friends, about 75 words.

The campfire crackles and sparks fly up into the dark. We sit in a circle with our faces glowing orange, and our shadows dance on the grass. Someone roasts corn on a stick, and the smell makes everyone hungry. Another friend tells a ghost story in a low voice. We laugh and shiver together. Above us, the sky is full of stars, and the night feels warm.
A diary page of about 60 words by a student who has just got her exam results and is relieved and happy.

Dear Diary,
Today the results came out. My hands were shaking as I opened the paper, and then I saw my marks. I had passed well! I felt so relieved that I almost cried. My parents hugged me, and my teacher smiled when I told her. I was so afraid for nothing. Tonight I will sleep peacefully, without a single worry.
About 65 words in diary form, please, from a teenage girl who babysat her baby cousin for the first time and found it harder than she expected.

Dear Diary,
Today I looked after my baby cousin for the first time. I thought it would be easy, but it was not! He cried when his mother left, and I did not know what to do. I sang songs, made faces and walked around the room with him. Finally, he fell asleep on my shoulder. I was so tired, but happy. Babysitting is real work!
My grandfather taught me chess today. Write a diary entry in my voice, about 70 words, that shows I lost but enjoyed it.

Dear Diary,
Today my grandfather taught me chess. He placed the board between us and explained how each piece moves. We played a game, and I lost very quickly. He did not mind, and he smiled kindly when I made a silly move. Even though I lost, I enjoyed it very much. I asked him for another game tomorrow, and he said yes. I think I will love this game.
A boy joined the school choir today and felt shy at first. Write his diary entry, about 80 words.

Dear Diary,
Today I joined the school choir. At first I felt shy and stood at the back, hoping nobody would notice me. When the teacher played the first note, everyone began to sing, and I quietly joined in. Slowly I forgot to be nervous. By the end, I was standing with the others and singing loudly. It felt good to be part of a group. I will go again next week.
Write about 70 words in diary style for a child who saw the sea for the very first time on a family trip.

Dear Diary,
Today I saw the sea for the first time! It was much bigger than I had imagined. The waves rolled in and out, and the water was so blue. I took off my shoes and let the foam tickle my toes. Father held my hand when a big wave came. I picked up shells and put them in my pocket. I never want to leave.
Here's an idea: a story of about 100 words about a scarecrow who is lonely in a field until a little girl begins to talk to him each day. It must end with her bringing him a new hat.

A scarecrow stood alone in a wheat field. Birds sat on his arms and laughed at him. He felt very lonely. One morning a little girl walked by and said, "Good morning!" She came every day after that, telling him about her school and her friends. The scarecrow could not answer, but he listened happily. When winter came, his old hat was torn and the wind blew it away. The next day the girl came running with a bright new hat. "This is for you," she said, and smiled.
I'd like a story of about 90 words about a boy who is always losing his pencil. One day he finds a tiny door in the desk. End with him finding his lost pencils inside.

Ravi lost a pencil every single day. His teacher sighed, and his mother stopped buying them. One morning, Ravi noticed a tiny door in the corner of his desk. He knocked softly, and it creaked open. Inside was a small room, and in it were all his missing pencils, stacked like firewood. A tiny voice said, "Please be more careful!" Ravi laughed and took them back. After that, he kept his pencil in his bag, and he never lost another one.
Tell a story, about 85 words, about a bus driver who waits for an old lady running towards the bus stop, even though he is late. End with her giving him a sweet.

The bus driver glanced at his watch. He was already late, and the passengers were restless. Then he saw an old lady hurrying towards the bus stop, holding her bag and a stick. She waved, out of breath. The driver sighed, then smiled and stopped the bus. She climbed in slowly, and the passengers made room for her. "Thank you, son," she said, and fished a sweet out of her bag. The driver took it with a grin. The day seemed a little brighter after that.
Give me a short story, about 90 words, that begins with a clock running backwards. Give it a gentle twist ending: it turns out he was looking at its reflection in a mirror.

One morning, Kavi noticed the big clock in the hall was running backwards. The hands turned slowly the wrong way. "Is time going back?" he wondered. He ran to tell his grandmother, who laughed and said, "Look again." Kavi stared at the clock, then turned his head. He had been looking at a mirror. The clock in it was only a reflection. The real clock, on the wall behind him, was ticking normally. Kavi felt a little silly, and then laughed with his grandmother.
Write a story, about 100 words, about a village lantern festival where a small boy's lantern keeps going out, but a girl helps him. It should end with both lanterns floating up together.

At the village lantern festival, everyone carried a glowing lantern to the river. Little Ashok held his own, but a breeze blew it out again and again. He felt sad as the other lanterns floated away. A girl standing nearby saw him and came over. "Let me help," she said. She cupped her hands around his lantern and lit it again with her own. Together they walked to the water and set both lanterns on the river. They floated up in the warm night, side by side, and Ashok smiled.
For a school newsletter, about 70 words on why reading the newspaper is good for older students.

Reading a newspaper helps older students understand the world around them. It tells us what is happening in our city, our country and far-off places. It also builds our vocabulary and helps us form our own opinions. Even ten minutes a day makes a difference. You might discover a sport, a hobby or a problem you want to help solve. Start with one page that interests you, and then read more.
Why do cities need trees? Write a paragraph of about 80 words for a class essay.

Cities need trees because they make life better for everyone. Trees give shade, and they keep the streets cooler on hot days. They give homes to birds and small animals. Their leaves clean the air a little and make the streets look beautiful. A walk under trees is calmer than a walk on a bare road. When cities plan new roads and buildings, they should save the trees and plant many more.
Why does saying sorry take courage? Write about 70 words for teenagers.

Saying sorry is harder than it sounds. It means admitting that you made a mistake, and that can feel uncomfortable. You may worry that the other person will be angry or that you will look weak. But an honest apology shows strength. It tells people that you care about them more than your pride. It can mend a friendship and make you feel lighter. Be brave and say it.
Give me four lines of verse about waves on the shore.

The waves roll in, then roll away,
They write on sand and wash the day.
The shells are left in a silver line,
And the sea sings softly, calm and fine.
Write a six-line rhyme for children about a tiffin box that holds a surprise.

My tiffin box is shiny and round,
It rattles with a lovely sound.
At lunch I lift the lid up high,
And see a treat that makes me sigh.
A yummy paratha, warm and neat,
Mother's love makes lunch so sweet.
Write a gentle four-line lullaby for a sleepy puppy.

Close your eyes, my little pup,
The day is done, the moon is up.
Dream of bones and meadows wide,
Safe and warm right by my side.
My cousin has her classical dance exam tomorrow. Write a good-luck message for her, about 50 words.

Dear cousin,
Good luck for your dance exam tomorrow! You have practised so hard, and I have seen how gracefully you move. Just breathe, smile and enjoy it, as you always do. I am cheering for you, and I know you will shine on that stage.
With love
Our food took more than an hour to arrive at a restaurant, and nobody explained why. Write a polite complaint to the manager, about 55 words.

Dear Manager,
We visited your restaurant recently, and our food took more than an hour to arrive. Nobody explained the reason or offered an apology, even though we asked twice. We like your food and would like to return, but this wait was very long. I hope you will look into it and improve your service.
Yours sincerely
Our coach gave us extra practice sessions on weekends for the whole month. Write a thank-you note from me to him, about 45 words.

Dear Coach,
Thank you for the extra practice sessions on weekends this month. You gave up your free time for us, and we have noticed how much better we play. Your patience and encouragement mean a lot to all of us. We are very grateful.
Your player
I submitted my homework two days late because of a family function. Write a polite sorry note to my teacher, about 45 words.

Dear Teacher,
I am sorry that I submitted my homework two days late. We had a family function at home, and I could not find the time. I should have told you earlier. It will not happen again. Thank you for your understanding.
Yours obediently
My sister-in-law Pallavi has just opened a small bakery. Write her a warm congratulations message, about 50 words.

Dear Pallavi,
Congratulations on opening your bakery! I know how long you dreamed of this, and now the smell of fresh bread will fill the street. Everyone in the family is proud of you. We will be your first customers. Best of luck for your new adventure.
With love
My friend Joel has a fever and cannot join our school trip. Write a cheerful get-well message, about 45 words.

Dear Joel,
We are sorry you cannot come on the trip. It will not be the same without you! Please rest and get well soon. We will take lots of photos and tell you every funny thing that happens. See you soon!
Your friends
Write a reminder to my team that our Wednesday potluck lunch is on, and everyone should bring one dish. About 40 words, in a cheerful tone.

Hi team,
A cheerful reminder that our potluck lunch is on Wednesday! Please bring one dish to share. It can be anything you like, sweet or savoury. Let us enjoy good food together and a little break from work. See you there!
Cheers
Please write a short thank-you note, about 50 words, to the cleaning staff at our school for keeping the classrooms spotless all year.

Dear cleaning staff,
Thank you for keeping our classrooms and corridors so clean all year. Your hard work often goes unnoticed, but it makes our school a pleasant place to learn. We appreciate everything you do. We promise to keep our desks and floors tidy too.
From the students
I promised to take my little sister to the park on Sunday but did not, because I was busy with homework. Write a sorry note to her, about 50 words.

Dear sister,
I am sorry that I did not take you to the park on Sunday. I know you were waiting, and I broke my promise. I had too much homework, but I should have told you earlier. Let us go this Saturday, and we can have ice cream too.
Your brother
Class 5 performed a play at the school assembly today. Write a congratulations message from their teacher, about 55 words.

Dear Class 5,
Congratulations on your wonderful play at the assembly today! You remembered your lines, spoke clearly and acted with great feeling. The audience enjoyed every moment. I am very proud of each one of you, including those who worked behind the stage. Well done, and thank you for your effort.
Your teacher
Remind my roommate to lock the door when she leaves for work and take the spare key. Short and polite, about 30 words.

Hi,
A quick reminder: please lock the door when you leave for work and take the spare key with you. I will be out all day. Thank you!
Your roommate
My friend's father drove me home late at night when the buses had stopped. Write a thank-you message to him, about 45 words.

Dear Sir,
Thank you for driving me home last night when the buses had stopped. It was late, and I was worried about how I would get home. I am thankful for your kindness and for making sure I reached safely. Please accept my sincere thanks.
Regards
Help me write a farewell party invitation, about 50 words, for my classmate who is moving abroad. The party will be on Friday at lunch break, in the school garden.

Dear friends,
Our classmate is moving abroad, and we want to give him a farewell he will never forget! Please join us on Friday at the lunch break in the school garden. We will share snacks, take photos and write messages for him. Come and say goodbye with smiles.
From your classmates
A new colleague joined our team this week. Write an invitation, about 45 words, to a welcome tea in the pantry on Thursday at 4 pm.

Dear team,
Please join us for a welcome tea this Thursday at 4 pm in the pantry. Our new colleague has just joined us, and we would like to say hello over tea and snacks. Come along and make our newest team member feel at home.
Our school is holding a drawing competition for Children's Day. Write a notice-style invitation, about 50 words, for students of Classes 3 to 5.

Drawing Competition for Children's Day!
Students of Classes 3 to 5 are invited to take part in a drawing competition to celebrate Children's Day. Bring your own colours and show us your imagination. Prizes will be given to the best drawings. Please give your name to your class teacher to enrol.
Art Department
I'd love to invite my friends to a cycling ride on Sunday morning that starts at the park gate at 6 am and ends with breakfast. Write it in about 55 words.

Hi friends,
Let us go for a cycling ride this Sunday morning! We will meet at the park gate at 6 am and ride together. When we are done, we will stop for a hearty breakfast. Please bring your cycle and a bottle of water. It will be great fun. Hope you can come!
My cousin is getting married and the mehndi evening is on Thursday at 6 pm at our house. Write an invitation to the girls in the family, about 50 words.

Dear girls,
Our cousin's wedding is near, and we are holding a mehndi evening at our house this Thursday at 6 pm. Come and put beautiful designs on your hands, sing and dance with us, and enjoy the sweets. Wear something colourful. It would not be a celebration without all of you!
With love
We ordered a birthday cake for my daughter and it arrived stale. Write a polite complaint to the bakery, about 55 words, and ask for a replacement or refund.

Dear Sir or Madam,
We ordered a cake from your bakery for my daughter's birthday. It arrived stale, and we could not serve it to our guests. We were very disappointed, as it was an important day for her. I request you to either replace the cake or give us a refund. Thank you for your attention.
Yours faithfully
The branches of my neighbour's tree are blocking the light into my window. Write a friendly request, about 55 words, asking him to trim them.

Dear Neighbour,
I hope you are well. I wanted to mention that the branches of your tree have grown across my window and are blocking much of the light. Would you be willing to trim them when you have a moment? I would be very grateful. Please let me know if I can help in any way.
Warm regards
I'm a student who wants to use the school computer lab for an hour after class on weekdays. Write a polite request to the principal, about 60 words.

Dear Principal,
I am a student of this school, and I would like to use the computer lab for an hour after class on weekdays. I want to practise typing and finish my project work, as I do not have a computer at home. May I kindly request your permission? Thank you for your consideration.
Yours obediently
A taxi driver took a very long route and charged me far more than I expected. Write a polite complaint, about 60 words, to the taxi company.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I recently took a taxi from your company, and the driver took a very long route to my destination. As a result, the fare was far more than I had expected. I would like to request you to look into this and explain how the fare was calculated. I look forward to your response.
Yours faithfully
A mechanic repaired my bicycle but the brakes still do not work well. Write a polite complaint, about 50 words, asking him to fix it properly.

Dear Sir,
I gave my bicycle to your shop for repair, but the brakes still do not work well. This makes it unsafe to ride. I request you to please check them again and fix them properly. I am happy to bring the bicycle back whenever it suits you. Thank you.
Yours sincerely
Draft an email to my professor asking for a short appointment next week to discuss my project topic, in about 55 words.

Subject: Request for an appointment

Dear Professor,
I would like to discuss my project topic with you and would be grateful for a short appointment next week. Please tell me which day and time suit you best. I will bring a short outline of my ideas. Thank you for your time and guidance.
Yours sincerely
Tell everyone in the office, by email, that from Monday, lunch will start at 1 pm instead of 12.30 pm. Keep it to about 40 words.

Subject: New lunch timing

Dear all,
Please note that from Monday, lunch will start at 1 pm instead of 12.30 pm. Kindly plan your meetings accordingly. If this causes any problem, please let me know. Thank you for your cooperation.
Regards
There is a broken footpath near our market where people keep tripping. Write a letter to the editor of a local newspaper, about 65 words, asking the authorities to repair it.

To the Editor,
I am writing about the broken footpath near our local market. Many people, including older citizens and children, trip over its broken stones every day. It has been like this for a long time. I request the authorities to repair the footpath soon, before somebody gets hurt. I hope that, with your help, this issue will get the attention it needs.
Yours faithfully
Write a friendly email to my class group asking everyone to send me their photos from last week's trip, about 50 words, by Sunday evening.

Subject: Photos from the trip

Hi everyone,
I hope you all enjoyed last week's trip as much as I did! Could you please send me the photos you took? I would like to make a small album for the class. Please send them by Sunday evening. Thank you!
Cheers
Our society is organising a blood donation camp on Sunday from 9 am to 1 pm in the clubhouse. Write a notice, about 45 words, inviting healthy adults to take part.

NOTICE
A blood donation camp will be held in the clubhouse this Sunday from 9 am to 1 pm. Healthy adult residents are warmly invited to take part. Your donation can help a person in need. Please come with your identity card. Thank you for your generosity.
Society Committee
Create a notice, about 45 words, that registrations for the inter-house quiz are open until Friday. Students should give names to their house captain.

NOTICE
Registrations for the inter-house quiz are open until Friday. Students who wish to take part should give their names to their house captain. Each house may send a team of interested students. Please prepare well and enjoy the quiz.
Quiz Committee
The school canteen is adding a new snack menu from Monday. Write a short notice, about 40 words, for the board.

NOTICE
From Monday, the school canteen will offer a new snack menu. There will be fresh sandwiches, fruit and other tasty items to choose from. Students are welcome to try them during the break. Please carry your canteen coupons or enough change.
Canteen Management
School library notice, please: it will be closed on Thursday for stocktaking and will reopen on Friday. About 35 words.

NOTICE
The school library will be closed on Thursday for stocktaking. It will reopen on Friday at the usual time. Students who need books may borrow them before Thursday. We apologise for the inconvenience.
Librarian
Describe a tea garden on a misty hillside in about 70 words.

The tea garden rolls down the hillside in neat green rows. Mist drifts between the bushes, and the air is cool and damp. Women in bright clothes move along the rows, picking the top leaves with quick fingers and dropping them into baskets on their backs. A thin path winds between the bushes. Everything smells of fresh leaves, and the whole hill seems to be breathing softly.
Describe a pond full of lotus flowers early in the morning, in about 60 words.

Pink lotus flowers rest on a still green pond. Large round leaves float like plates, and drops of water roll across them like silver beads. A dragonfly lands on a bud and takes off again. A faint ripple spreads across the water where a fish has risen. The early light is soft, and the pond looks like a quiet, secret garden.
Write a description of an ancient banyan tree in a village square in about 80 words.

The old banyan tree stands in the middle of the village square. Its thick branches spread wide, and long roots hang down like ropes. Beneath it is a stone platform where elders sit and talk, and children play hide and seek around the trunk. Birds nest in its leaves, and a cool shade covers everyone below. It has seen many generations come and go, and it still stands quietly, as if listening to every story.
How would you describe a school assembly on a cold morning? Give me about 70 words.

On a cold winter morning, the children gather in neat rows on the ground. Their breath makes small clouds in the air, and many have woollen caps pulled down over their ears. The teacher at the microphone leads the prayer, and the children's voices rise together. A few shiver and stamp their feet. When the national anthem finishes, they rush to class, glad to be warm again.
Describe the sound of rain on a tin roof in about 55 words.

The first raindrops land on the tin roof with soft taps. Soon the taps become a rapid drumbeat, and the whole roof seems to sing. Inside, the sound fills the room and makes every other noise disappear. It is a loud, steady, friendly music that makes me feel snug and sleepy. I pull my blanket up and listen.
My sister and I adopted two kittens today. Write my diary entry, about 65 words, with some of our funny first moments.

Dear Diary,
Today we brought home two kittens! One is grey and the other is ginger. At first they hid under the bed, and we had to coax them out with a saucer of milk. Then the ginger one chased my shoelace around the room, and the grey one climbed onto my sister's head. We laughed so much. I think this house will never be quiet again!
Summer holidays begin today. Write a diary entry, about 70 words, from a child on this first day, who is unsure how to fill the days.

Dear Diary,
Today was the first day of the summer holidays. I woke up late and ate a long breakfast, and then I did not know what to do. No school bag, no bell, no homework. It felt strange and wonderful. I made a list of things to try, like painting, reading and flying a kite. Let us see how many I can do!
Today I did a magic trick for my family and it worked. Give me about 60 words of diary writing about it, in the voice of a ten-year-old.

Dear Diary,
Today I performed my first magic trick in front of my whole family! I made a coin disappear and then found it behind my sister's ear. Everyone gasped, and my grandfather asked me to do it again. I was so nervous that my hands shook, but the trick worked. I felt like a real magician. I will practise some more.
Here is a diary entry I need, about 65 words, from a girl who cleaned out her cupboard and found her favourite old toy.

Dear Diary,
Today I cleaned my cupboard, and I found my old stuffed rabbit at the very back. His ear was a bit torn, but he looked just the same. I remember carrying him everywhere when I was little. I sat on the floor and hugged him for a long time. I will not give him away. I put him on my bed.
A boy won second prize in a drawing competition at school today. Write his diary entry, about 60 words, showing he is proud but wishes he had won first.

Dear Diary,
Today I won second prize in the school drawing competition! My teacher shook my hand, and my friends clapped. I felt proud, but a tiny part of me wished it was first prize. When I saw the winning drawing, I understood why it won. It was really lovely. Next year I will work even harder and try again.
Tell a story of about 80 words about a rooster who forgets how to crow, and a little girl who helps him remember. End with the sun rising on cue.

Every morning, the rooster crowed to wake up the village. But one day he opened his beak, and nothing came out. He felt so ashamed that he hid in the barn. A little girl found him there. "Don't worry," she said gently. "Try again." She stood beside him and crowed softly herself. The rooster stretched his neck, took a deep breath and let out a loud, proud cock-a-doodle-doo! At that very moment, the sun rose over the hills.
Write a gentle story, about 85 words, about a boy who buries a coin in the garden, hoping a money tree will grow. Instead, it should end with him learning to enjoy a different surprise: a sunflower.

Mohan was told that anything planted in the soil will grow. So he buried a shiny coin in the garden, hoping for a tree full of money. Every day he watered the spot and waited. Weeks passed, and nothing sprouted. He felt foolish. One morning, he noticed a green shoot a short distance away. It grew taller and taller, until a bright yellow sunflower opened. Mohan smiled. It was not the tree he wanted, but it was a better surprise, and it made him very happy.
I'd like a story of about 90 words about the moon visiting a small girl who cannot sleep. It should end with the girl falling asleep.

Mira lay awake, staring at the ceiling. Suddenly, a silver beam slipped through her window. It was the moon, who had come down to see why she was not asleep. "I am scared of the dark," whispered Mira. "But I am here," said the moon softly. "I light the night for everyone." She smiled and felt less afraid. The moon sat quietly beside her window, glowing. Mira closed her eyes and listened to the quiet, and soon, she was fast asleep.
Tell a story, about 100 words, about a rickshaw puller who finds a bag left behind by a passenger and returns it. End with the passenger thanking him warmly.

Raju pulled his rickshaw through the busy streets all day. One evening he noticed a bag on the back seat, left behind by his last passenger. He looked inside and saw only clothes and papers. He did not know the passenger's name, so he went back to the stand where he had picked him up and waited. An hour later, the worried passenger came running. Raju held up the bag. The man smiled with relief and thanked him again and again. "You are an honest man," he said.
Two ants meet on a leaf floating down a stream. Write a children's story, about 85 words, about how they work together to reach the bank.

Two ants were riding on a leaf down a stream, when the leaf started to spin. One ant said, "We must reach the bank!" The other said, "But the water is deep." They looked around and saw a twig hanging low near the shore. The first ant held the leaf steady, and the second ant stretched out and caught the twig. Then they pulled the leaf closer, together. At last, they stepped onto dry land, happy and tired.
Write 70 words on why curiosity helps us learn, for a class assembly.

Curiosity is the wish to know more. When we ask questions and wonder why things happen, we learn much faster than when we simply memorise. Curious children read more, try new things and are not afraid of mistakes. Great discoveries began with someone asking, "What if?" So never be shy to ask a question in class. Your curiosity can take you far.
For a youth magazine, about 70 words on why listening is as important as speaking in a friendship.

Listening is as important as speaking in a friendship. When you listen, you show your friend that you care about what they feel. People open up when they know someone is paying attention. Without listening, we only hear our own voice, and misunderstandings grow. Good friends take turns speaking and listening. Next time a friend talks, put down your phone and really hear them.
Write a short paragraph, about 65 words, about why a sense of humour helps in hard times, for a school magazine.

A sense of humour helps us in difficult times. When we laugh at a small mistake or a silly situation, our worries feel lighter. Laughter also brings people closer, because we share a happy moment. It does not mean we ignore problems. It means we face them with a smile and keep going. Even on a bad day, one good laugh can change the mood.
A four-line poem for my mother, please, about her lap being the safest place in the world.

Your lap is where I always rest,
It is the place I love the best.
When I am sad or tired or small,
Your arms will catch me if I fall.
Write a short rhyme, six lines, for children about a clock that is always in a hurry.

Tick-tock, tick-tock, the clock is fast,
It wants the hours to rush on past.
It hurries round the numbered face,
In a very, very, very big race.
The clock is quick, it cannot wait,
So hurry up, or you'll be late!
Make up a funny four-line poem about a monkey who steals a hat.

A cheeky monkey stole my hat,
And wore it proudly, just like that.
He tipped it, bowed and climbed a tree,
And now it fits him better than me.
Our Class 4 will present an assembly on Friday at 9 am about saving electricity. Please write a short invitation to parents, about 50 words.

Dear Parents,
Class 4 will present the school assembly this Friday at 9 am, and the topic is saving electricity. The children have worked hard on songs, a short play and some useful tips. Please come and watch. Your presence will encourage them. We look forward to seeing you.
Class 4 Teacher
